articleTitle: Understanding the spectral response of fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)

articleTitle: Facility management and restoration in the optical vs. data layers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. The promise of multi-terabit Internet protocol (IP) routers with high-speed interfaces matching per-wavelength line rate in a DWDM system raises the specter of direct IP over DWM network architecture which usurps traditional transport layer functions. In this paper we will examine economic as well as operation aspects of this architecture against the architecture in which an active optical layer provides wavelength level switching and management functions.

articleTitle: Novel micromechanical network elements
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. Innovative optical microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) having valuable loss, speed, size and cost attributes, offer new solutions to the design and operation of lightwave network elements. The range of function and complexity achieved in optical MEMS devices is illustrated by examples of deflecting-membrane attenuators and equalizers, single-element 1/spl times/2 switches, reconfigurable multi-channel add/drop multiplexers, and large-scale micromechanical integrated circuit switch arrays.

articleTitle: Fiber issues for nontraditional wavelength bands
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. The rapid increase in bandwidth demand is driving systems toward utilizing more of the roughly 50 THz optical bandwidth available in a fiber. This paper explores fiber issues and system opportunities for using wavelengths outside the traditional 1310 and 1550 nm windows, including the L-band the S-band, and, with new zero-OH fibers, the 1400 nm region.

articleTitle: HFC architecture for broadband two-way access
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk will cover the evolution of the hybrid fiber coax (HFC) network from a one-way medium for the broadcast of analog video into a high-speed two-way data network. Particular emphasis to the next generation of HFC networks.

articleTitle: Data intensive IP transport nets
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. Explosive growth in the demand for bandwidth continues and there are no signs of slowing down. Along with higher capacity there is a demand for better bandwidth utilization and management, faster provisioning and new value added services. These demands could be met by taking the best of layers 3/2 recent advancements and combining them with the strengths of layer 1 technologies. This talk evaluates the next generation Internet protocol architecture that will efficiently support data intensive network demands of the future.

articleTitle: Fiber optic manifolding in RF systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. I describe the utilization of RF photonic manifolds for signal gathering and beam steering applications in antenna systems. We focus on the receiver architecture for radars and communication systems and how photonic downconversion, LO distribution and beamsteering are applied.

articleTitle: Traffic model for USA long-distance optical network
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Voice, transaction data, and Internet traffic models are developed and used to estimate the traffic demand and growth between major US cities. Shortest path routing is used to estimate the capacity required on individual links, as well as traffic granularity and the fraction of traffic dropped at each city.

articleTitle: Block turbo code performances for long-haul DWDM optical transmission systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the performance of a foward error correction (fec) scheme for submarine transmission systems using Block turbo code. The decoding is based on soft decoding and soft decision. This solution gives 4 dB additional gain margin compared with the existing rs(255,239) with redundancy equal to 28%.

articleTitle: Transparent optical networking in backbone networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The explosive growth of Internet traffic is stressing both the transport and processing capabilities of backbone networks. Transparent optical networking employing ultra-long-reach dense-WDM transport and all-optical cross-connects is shown to provide a scalable and economic solution to this problem.

articleTitle: Making use of a two stage multiplexing scheme in a WDM network
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The paper explores the implications of using a two stage optical multiplexing scheme in optical WDM nodes. This allows to keep bands of adjacent wavelengths intact, thereby reducing the cost of multiplexing, increasing the number of hops and simplifying network management.

articleTitle: Fully provisioned 112/spl times/112 micro-mechanical optical crossconnect with 35.8 Tb/s demonstrated capacity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A scalable, fully provisioned 112/spl times/112 micro-mechanical optical cross connect with mean insertion loss of 7.5 dB@1550 nm into single-mode optical fiber and <10 ms switching speed is presented. 35.8 Tbit/s aggregate capacity was demonstrated with 320 Gbit/s TDM signals signals.

articleTitle: Compact optical cross-connect switch based on total internal reflection in a fluid-containing planar lightwave circuit
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical cross-connect switch matrices have demonstrated transmission losses of 0.07 dB per crosspoint, crosstalk of /spl sim/70 dB per crosspoint and switching times of 1 msec. We now have the technology to produce 32/spl times/32-size matrices.

articleTitle: An analysis of the improvements in OSNR from distributed Raman amplifiers using modern transmission fibres
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present measurements of the Raman efficiency spectra for recent transmission fibres and model the improvement in DWDM system performance using distributed Raman amplification. For 5 spans of 25 dB fibre loss and 1 dB of connector loss, we predict 4.5-6.5 dB improvement in optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR) when using a 500 mW pump, a variation of up to 2 dB depending on fibre type.

articleTitle: A programmable polarization-mode dispersion emulator for systematic testing of 10 Gb/s PMD compensators
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A programmable polarization-mode dispersion emulator is demonstrated first and higher-order PMD is systematically generated. Twelve birefringent crystals with 10 ps differential-group-delay apiece are mounted in twelve computer controlled motorized rotating stages.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion emulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate a new technique to realistically emulate polarization mode dispersion. We demonstrate that 15 sections of polarization-maintaining fiber with randomly rotatable connections emulates an almost ideal Maxwellian differential group delay (DGD) distribution, whereas fixed connections is inadequate.

articleTitle: A novel optical signal-to-noise ratio monitoring technique for WDM networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel optical signal-to-noise (OSNR) monitoring technique based on receiver noise analysis. The results show that the accuracy of the proposed technique is better than 1 dB when the OSNR was 16-28 dB.

articleTitle: Reduction of the chromatic dispersion penalty at 10 Gbit/s by integrated electronic equalisers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: At 10 Gbit/s a 3.3 dB reduction of the power penalty induced by the chromatic dispersion of an 127 km standard single-mode fiber (G.652) has been achieved (BER=10/sup -9/, PRBS 2/sup 23/-1) by processing the detected signal in the receiver with a nonlinear equaliser realized as SiGe integrated circuit.

articleTitle: Cost effective performance monitoring in WDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Cost effective methods utilizing variable thresholds in the receiver IC to determine histograms for optical performance monitoring are presented. Measurements which show the possibility to monitor the dispersion with these methods are shown.

articleTitle: Review of wideband hybrid amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The configurations and characteristics of several types of wideband hybrid amplifiers are presented. Each of the amplifiers consists of an EDFA and a Raman amplifier (distributed or discrete type) and yields low noise in WDM systems.

articleTitle: Fast and fine wavelength tuning of a GCSR laser using a digitally controlled driver
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate fast (4 ns) and fine (0.8 nm/step) wavelength tuning of a grating coupler sampled reflector (GCSR) laser, using the laser fs reflector section and a novel digitally-controlled driver, for application in future WDM packet switched networks.

articleTitle: Compact high-power wavelength selectable lasers for WDM applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Wavelength selectable lasers with record +1O dBm fiber coupled output power and uniform characteristics have been realized by integration of eight-channel distributed feedback laser arrays with low-loss multi-mode interference combiners and optical amplifiers with a length of only 2 mm.

articleTitle: Ultrafast, high-power 1.55 /spl mu/m side-illuminated photodetector with integrated spot size converter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: 40 Gbit/s photodetectors require high bandwidth at high power levels, as supplied by waveguide-integrated p-i-n diodes on InP. By monolithic integration of a spot size transformer a responsivity of 0.5 A/W is achieved and fiber alignment tolerances are increased by one order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of chromatic dispersion in various types of optical fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Temperature dependence of chromatic dispersion is examined for various types of fibers. Its coefficient is found strongly dependent on dispersion slope, indicating that low dispersion slope transmission lines are desirable for future high bit-rate transmission.

articleTitle: WDM burst switching for petabit data networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: WDM burst switching combines optical data paths and electronic control to enable very high capacity routing switches. This paper shows how expected advances in optical component technology and electronics can lead to petabit capacity IP routers.

articleTitle: Cancellation of all Kerr nonlinearities in long fiber spans using a LiNbO/sub 3/ phase conjugator and Raman amplification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A LiNbO/sub 3/ phase-conjugator and Raman pumping in fiber are used in order to cancel all Kerr nonlinearities in long fiber spans. We demonstrate this effect in single and multichannel transmission at 10, 40, and 100 Gb/s.

articleTitle: PMD mitigation techniques and their effectiveness in installed fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The main building blocks of adaptive PMD compensators, the equalizer, the eye monitor for feedback signal generation, and the distortion tracking and adaptation logic for equalizer control will be reviewed with regard to system implementation. Equalizer units based on optical, optoelectronic, and electrical compensation schemes are discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical optimization of residual dispersion in dispersion-managed systems at 40 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Through numerical simulations, we optimize the amount of residual chromatic dispersion in 40 Gbit/s single-channel links. It is found proportional to the nonlinear phase, and independent on fiber local dispersion and dispersion map.

articleTitle: Contention resolution in optical packet-switching networks: under long-range dependent traffic
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate the efficiency of contention resolution techniques such as optical buffering, wavelength conversion and multi-path routing in optical packet-switching routers under long-range dependent traffic. New techniques are required to improve the router performance.

articleTitle: Photonic IP routing using optical codes: 10 Gbit/s optical packet transfer experiment
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Packets consisting of 8-chip-long header and 64 bit-long burst payload data at 10 Gbit/s are generated and IP (Internet protocol) routed optical domain, based upon photonic processings of the optically coded address. All-optical packet address inspection and 10 Gbit/s burst payload data transportation are demonstrated experimentally for the first time.

articleTitle: Dispersive multiplexing in multimode fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel multiplexing technique for multimode fiber is presented. The technique uses modal dispersion to dramatically increase the information capacity of multimode fiber. A simple proof-of-principle experiment is shown that demonstrates the feasibility of this idea.

articleTitle: Wavelength-selective coupler and add-drop multiplexer using long-period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a low-insertion-loss wavelength-selective coupler that uses cladding-mode coupling between two identical fibers. The device is simple to manufacture, has >40 dB of channel isolation and no back-reflection.

articleTitle: 1800 Gb/s transmission of one hundred and eighty 10 Gb/s WDM channels over 7000 km using the full EDFA C-band
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: One hundred and eighty 10 Gb/s WDM channels were transmitted over 7000 km in 43 nm of optical bandwidth with a maximum spectral efficiency of 0.4 (bits/s)/Hz. Error free performance was measured for all channels using an advanced error correcting code.

articleTitle: Broadband CW pumped fiber optical parametric amplifier with 49 dB gain and wavelength conversion efficiency
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Broadband, CW pumped fiber-based parametric amplifier with 49 dB of internal gain and wavelength conversion efficiency, corresponding to a net gain/efficiency of 38 dB, is demonstrated. BER measurements indicate performance comparable to EDFAs. These amplifiers may thus find new applications in future lightwave systems.

articleTitle: 320 Gbit/s single-channel pseudo-linear transmission over 200 km of nonzero-dispersion fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Single-channel transmission at 320 Gbit/s is demonstrated over record length of 200 km (2/spl times/100 km) of nonzero-dispersion fiber. Semiconductor based transmitter, demultiplexer and clock recovery is employed as well as uncorrelated multiplexing in the transmitter.

articleTitle: High-performance, manufacturable avalanche photodiodes for 10 Gb/s optical receivers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We describe an InGaAs-InP avalanche photodiode employing a shaped diffusion profile and floating guard rings. High gain-bandwidth products (85 to 95 GHz), 10 GHz peak bandwidths, high gains (50 to 100), and good gain uniformity (/spl plusmn/4%) are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A proof-of-concept, ultra-low latency optical label switching testbed demonstration for next generation Internet networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical label switching testbed has been demonstrated to realize an NGI network with ultra-low latency, simplified protocol stacks, and data transparency. Packet applications have been successfully sent, with less than 1 msec switching node delay, over a label-switched network.

articleTitle: Investigation and design rules of supercontinuum sources for WDM applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate supercontinuum generation (SC) in normal dispersion fiber in order to assess the feasibility of WDM transmitters based on SC sources. The interest of this case lies in its relative simplicity, and in the high coherence of the SC spectrum that is obtained through this process. We demonstrate that seed pulse shape influences both SC spectrum flatness and its noise characteristics. Simple design rules for the maximum spectrum magnification and for the corresponding fiber length are proposed. We show numerically and experimentally that a proper design can keep the amplitude noise of the SC spectrum comparable with the amplitude noise of the seed pulse.

articleTitle: Fabrication of silica-on-Si waveguide with higher index difference and its application to 256 channel arrayed waveguide multi/demultiplexer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Improved techniques were used to fabricate a silica-on-Si waveguide with a higher core-to-cladding index difference and a 2 mm bending radius. A 256 channel and 25 GHz spacing arrayed-waveguide multiplexer with low loss and low crosstalk was successfully fabricated for the first time using the waveguides.

articleTitle: 40 GHz mode-locked SOA fiber ring laser with 20 nm tuning range
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 2.5 ps pulse width, 40 GHz repetition rate, 20 nm tuning range, mode-locked fiber ring laser is presented. The source mode-locks through gain saturation of its SOA from an external 5 GHz DFB diode.

articleTitle: Performance improvement in high capacity, ultra-long distance, WDM systems using forward error correction codes
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a performance study of a forward error correction (FEC) code using theoretical models, Monte-Carlo computer simulations, and a long-haul WDM transmission experiment. With a 14% redundancy code, the Q-factor was increased by 6.2 dB for both linear and non-linear impairments.

articleTitle: MEMS variable optical attenuator for DWDM optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A fully packaged variable optical attenuator for DWDM systems based on a MEMS silicon chip is shown to have low insertion loss, low PDL, a flat response over the wavelength range 1530 nm-1565 nm, and a low DC drive voltage.

articleTitle: High-spectral-efficiency transmission systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Spectrally-efficient transmission techniques provide the capability for higher channel density in WDM systems and, in some cases, allow the extension of the transmission distance limited by physical fiber impairments, such as chromatic dispersion and polarization mode dispersion. We review the main techniques and evaluate the potential of their implementation in dense WDM systems.

articleTitle: C-band tunable 6 mW vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate micro-electromechanical vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (MEM-VCSELs) that couple >6 mW of power into a single-mode fiber. These devices are continuously tunable across the entire c-band and offer error-free transmission over >500 km of single-mode fiber at OC-48 data rates.

articleTitle: Cost-effective depolarized diode pump unit designed for C-band flat-gain Raman amplifiers to control EDFA gain profile
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A cost-effective pumping unit with only two depolarized pump LDs for C-band flat-gain Raman amplifiers is proposed. The Raman gain in DCF is applied to simultaneously control the overall gain and gain flatness of an in-line EDFA.

articleTitle: Sixteen-channel wavelength selector monolithically integrated on InP
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 16-channel wavelength selector was realised by monolithic integration on InP of phased-array wavelength demultiplexers and semiconductor optical amplifiers. Zero fibre-to-fibre loss was obtained for 50 mA driving current.

articleTitle: Fused fiber optic variable attenuator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a fused fiber optic variable attenuator with a polymer sub-cladding layer. It exhibits a wide dynamic range of 1.5-45 dB, relatively flat wavelength response, and high thermal sensitivity of up to 3 dB//spl deg/C.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s signal transmission using optical 3R regenerator based on electroabsorption modulators
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The optical 3R regeneration based on electroabsorption modulators was successfully demonstrated at 40 Gbit/s. The 40 Gbit/s 3R optical transmission over 1000 km was carried out, for the first time, with excellent performance improvement.

articleTitle: 3.28 Tb/s (82/spl times/40 Gb/s) transmission over 3/spl times/100 km nonzero-dispersion fiber using dual C- and L-band hybrid Raman/erbium doped inline amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of a record aggregate capacity of 3.28 Tb/s (82/spl times/40 Gb/s PRBS 2/sup 31/-1 NRZ) over 3/spl times/100 km of a demonstration TrueWave(R) fiber with very low dispersion slope. The system for the first time incorporate dual C- and L-band transmission and distributed Raman amplification in addition to the 40 Gb/s line rate.

articleTitle: Dispersion and dispersion-slope compensation of NZDSF for 40 Gb/s operation over the entire C band
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous dispersion and dispersion-slope compensation of 240 km of nonzero dispersion shifted fibre (NZDSF) from 1530 to 1560 nm using a higher-order-mode-fiber compensator. With this compensator, 4O Gb/s operation is achieved across the band, in contrast to a several-nanometer window using conventional DCF.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion penalties associated with rotation of principal states of polarization in optical fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have measured the effect of rotation of the principal states of polarization (PSP) by using a dispersion-compensated system and focusing attention on wavelengths where the PSP rotation rate is large and the differential group delay is low.

articleTitle: Asymmetric WDM all-optical packet switched routers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: It is shown that asymmetric WDM all-optical routers architectures are the best candidates to reduce hardware volume and cost of all-optical networks. We show that due to the non-uniform network traffic behavior, routers require asymmetric wavelength conversion capabilities and also asymmetric buffering capacity to solve contention. This paper shows that due to the topology, packets may generate traffic bottlenecks produced by a tendency of the routing scheme to send packets with different destinations through preferred paths.

articleTitle: Novel all optical limiter using electroabsorption modulators
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel all optical limiter based on a wavelength-converter and a saturable-absorber using electroabsorption modulators has been proposed. Elimination of severe pattern-dependent intensity fluctuations in lO Gbit/s optical signals was successfully demonstrated with this new scheme.

articleTitle: Experimental nonlinear cancellation of polarization-mode dispersion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a nonlinear-canceller decision circuit to ameliorate the effects of polarization-mode dispersion. This integrated circuit adapts the receiver decision threshold to the intersymbol interference arising from previous bits. It is capable of reducing an infinite penalty to a 3 dB penalty.

articleTitle: A 104 GHz 328 fs soliton pulse train generation through a comb-like dispersion profiled fiber using short high nonlinearity dispersion fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have constructed a 693.6 m long comb-like dispersion profiled fiber using a newly developed high-nonlinearity DSF, through which a dual frequency beat signal was compressed by 14.7 times to generate a 104 GHz train of 328 fs pulses.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a media access protocol for HORNET: a WDM multiple access metropolitan area ring network
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a novel CSMA/CA protocol for HORNET: a WDM multiple access MAN ring. HORNET uses subcarrier multiplexed tones to govern access to wavelengths, and a fast-tunable transmitter to allow the node to transmit on all wavelengths.

articleTitle: A multi-channel dispersion slope compensating optical allpass filter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A multi-channel dispersion slope compensating filter based on a Gires-Tournois interferometer with a specially designed thin-film filter is presented. The allpass filter has low loss, and negligible birefringence.

articleTitle: Extension of polarization-mode dispersion limit using optical mitigation and phase-shaped binary transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The admitted polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) limit is around 15% of the bit-time. With our first-order PMD mitigator, this limit is multiplied by 2 for a non-return to zero signal, and by 3 for a phase-shaped binary transmission signal.

articleTitle: L-band erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: WDM systems are being planned that will use the long-wavelength (L-band) or extended (E-Band) band of the erbium-doped fiber in coordination with the conventional band (C-band). Appending the L-band will ultimately double the available transmission bandwidth and reduce impairments due to nonlinearities in the fiber plant. The development of L-band EDFAs is proceeding at an aggressive pace, and it is anticipated that these next generation amplifiers will have a significant impact on lightwave communication systems in the very near future. This paper introduces (1) the motivation for L-band amplifiers, (2) technical issues related to development of commercial amplifiers, and (3) fundamental differences between C-band and L-band behavior.

articleTitle: Field evaluation of an optical PMD compensator using an installed 10 Gbit/s system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report, for the first time, results correlating PMD compensation performance to system instantaneous differential group delay (DGD) over installed fibre. We also report accurate replication of the installed fibre PMD conditions in a laboratory providing accelerated PMD exploration.

articleTitle: Detuning characteristics of fiber Bragg grating stabilized 980 nm pump lasers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate wavelength detuning effects between ridge waveguide 980 nm pump laser-fiber Bragg grating (FBG) pairs. A design point suppressing single-mode to multi-mode switching under coherence collapse is experimentally and theoretically developed.

articleTitle: Smart routers-simple optics a network architecture for IP over WDM
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A simple, general IP/WDM node architecture is prototyped, concentrating intelligence for optical and electronic resource management in IP, and exposing to IP a simple interface to WDM's capabilities for configurable bandwidth.

articleTitle: 3.2 Tb/s-1500 km WDM transmission experiment using 64 nm hybrid repeater amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: 3.2 Tb/s (160/spl times/20 Gb/s) RZ signals were transmitted over 1500 km precisely-flattened dispersion managed line with the use of newly developed 64 nm hybrid amplifiers. This is the first demonstration of multi terabit/s, long distance transmission.

articleTitle: Optical domain performance monitoring
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The rapid evolution of terrestrial optical networks is driving the need for optical domain performance monitoring in order to provide the lowest transport cost per managed bit. This paper presents various techniques for monitoring optical signals between 3R interfaces in terms of their economic value to the network operator.

articleTitle: A multi-wavelength locker for WDM system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple technique to stabilize the wavelengths of WDM lasers using a synchronized etalon filter and a digital signal processing board. The results shows that the proposed technique could maintain the frequency stability of each WDM laser within 200 MHz.

articleTitle: System application of 40 GHz all-optical clock in a 40 Gbit/s optical 3R regenerator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new all-optical clock operating from 6 to 46 GHz is presented and tested in 40 Gbit/s soliton 3R regenerator. Error-free single-channel 40 Gbit/s loop transmission is demonstrated over more than 10000 km with word length up to 2/sup 23/-1.

articleTitle: Ultrafast locking optical clock for IP packet switching applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The locking time of an all-optical clock is investigated. Self-pulsating, DFB lasers with detuned gratings are applied the clock locks within 10 "one" bits (1 ns) to injected data packets and keeps synchronized for some hundred "zero" bits.

articleTitle: 99.9% reflectivity dispersion-less square-filter fibre Bragg gratings for high speed DWDM networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We reported linear-phase Bragg grating filters with greater than 99.9% reflectivity. The filters are designed to have useful a bandwidth of 75% on a 5O GHz grid spacing, and show no dispersion induced penalties over the full useful band when tested at 10 Gbit/s in a back-to-back configuration.

articleTitle: Ultra-dense terabit capacity WDM transmission in L-band
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report error-free transmission of 100 wavelength-division-multiplexed (WDM) 10 Gb/s channels with 25 GHz spacing over 400 km of non-zero dispersion shifted fiber. High spectral efficiency of 0.4 b/s/Hz was achieved combining distributed Raman and erbium-doped fiber amplifiers.

articleTitle: Comparison of different modulation formats in terrestrial systems with high polarization mode dispersion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We compare the performance of NRZ, RZ, dispersion-managed solitons, and pre-chirped RZ formats in the presence of high polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) for 10 Gbit/s terrestrial systems. Fiber nonlinearities and signal chirp interact with PMD-induced pulse distortion to generate clear trends in system power penalties. We show that chirped RZ pulses are more tolerant to high PMD values.

articleTitle: Transmission properties of chirped return-to-zero pulses and nonlinear intersymbol interference in 10 Gb/s WDM transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Computer simulations are used to analyze the evolution of chirped return-to-zero pulses in long-haul dispersion managed 10 Gb/s systems. We demonstrate that pulses in the channels that are offset from system's zero dispersion suffer significant spreading over several bit periods. In the presence of nonlinearity this effect sets the usable bandwidth of the system.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s PMD compensation field experiment over 452 km using Principal State Transmission method
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Polarization Mode Dispersion (PMD) in optical fibers is a major limiting factor for bit rates of 10 Gb/s and more. First-order PMD distorts the signal waveform because of a differential group delay (DGD) between two principal states of polarization defined in the fiber. The PMD compensation ability of the PST method has been demonstrated in high PMD fiber for 10 Gb/s transmission over 452 km of installed fiber. To the best of our knowledge, compensation on an installed single mode optical fiber (SMF) with an average DGD of 60 ps has been demonstrated for the first time. Stable operation of the PST method was confirmed in the presence of 2nd-order PMD through correlation of the measured DGD and bit error rate (BER).

articleTitle: Full complex transmission and reflection characterization of a Bragg grating in a single laser sweep
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Using an all-fiber network and a tunable laser, all four complex response spectra (two transmission and two reflection) of a Bragg grating or any linear fiber optic component may be measured in less than ten seconds with a single laser sweep.

articleTitle: 1.2 Tbit/s (30/spl times/42.7 Gbit/s ETDM optical channel) WDM transmission over 376 km with 125 km spacing using forward error correction and carrier-suppressed RZ format
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate 1.2 Tbit/s (30/spl times/42.7 Gbit/s electrical time division multiplexing (ETDM) optical channel) WDM transmission over three 125 km-spans (span loss: 31.5 dB average) using carrier-suppressed return-to-zero format and forward error corrections in 50 nm tellurite-based EDFA gain band.

articleTitle: Requirements of optical layer network restoration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper discusses restoration requirements of optical layer network (OLN). Restoration methods are compared in terms of speed and efficiency. Requirements of the client layer services are summarized, and inter-working between the client layer and the optical layer is discussed.

articleTitle: Optical add-drop multiplexing of 60 GHz millimeterwave signals in a WDM radio-on-fiber ring
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A full-duplex millimeterwave over fiber ring system consisting of two simple basestations is presented. The basestations are addressed using individual wavelengths. Bit error rates below 10-9 are achieved for 156 Mb/s down- and uplink data within the 60 GHz band simultaneously.

articleTitle: Full validation of an optical 3R regenerator at 20 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An optical 3R regenerator combining semiconductor optical amplifier-based Mach Zehnder interferometers is assessed at 20 Gbit/s. Inserted in a recirculation loop including 110 mm of dispersion shifted fibre, more than 200 regenerators have been cascaded.

articleTitle: Influence of the statistics on polarization-mode dispersion compensator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Using various PMD statistics, and including higher-order terms, the performance of a PMD compensator with a fixed differential group delay (DGD) is evaluated. It is shown that the so-called Maxwellian case is the worst case both without and with compensation. Therefore, the optimization of a PMD compensator can be carried out with the Maxwellian case only.

articleTitle: Dynamic add/drop of 8-of-16 10 Gb/s channels in 4/spl times/40 km semiconductor-optical-amplifier-based WDM system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate the benefits of near-linear SOA-amplified 4/spl times/40 km WDM transmission system. Eight out of sixteen 10 Gb/s channels are added or dropped (with only a 0.7 bB penalty in the remaining channels) over a wide range of time scales.

articleTitle: 2410 km all-optical network field trial with 10 Gb/s DWDM transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report the longest deployed ultra-long haul unregenerated terrestrial 10 Gb/s DWDM optical network system. Transmission length for 2410 km with typical terrestrial site spacing of 100 km. The system had extensive optical networking capability with 5 in-line sites able to add/drop 100% of the transmission capacity.

articleTitle: Designing WDM optical network for reliability: routing light paths efficiently for path protection
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have suggested two strategies for path protection in WDM networks-one for path protection without spare capacity sharing and one that allows the spare capacities to be shared. Heuristic algorithms for efficiently determining the working and protection light-paths have been proposed and their performances studied through simulations on a model of the ARPA-2 network.

articleTitle: Large effective area dispersion compensating fiber for cabled compensation of standard single mode fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Production of wideband dispersion and dispersion slope compensating fiber with 35 /spl mu/m/sup 2/ effective area and low attenuation is demonstrated. This fiber is optimized for cable deployment in a 1:1 length ratio with standard single mode fiber.

articleTitle: OSNR monitoring technique using polarization-nulling method
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report a simple technique based on the polarization-nulling method to monitor the optical signal-to-noise ratios (OSNR's) of WDM signals automatically. The results show that the OSNR's could be monitored with accuracy better than 0.6 dB.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s all-optical clock recovery using three section self-pulsation DFB lasers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: All-optical clock recovery at 40 Gb/s was realized using a three-section gain-coupled DFB laser. The locking range is 300 Mb/s at an injection power of 300 mW.

articleTitle: High performance fused-type mode selective coupler for two-mode fiber devices
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a high performance fused-type mode selective coupler that couples the LP11 mode of a two-mode fiber and the LP01 mode of a matching single-mode fiber, the phase-matching condition was satisfied by etching and pre-pulling of a two-mode fiber, the excess loss and the maximum coupling ratio of 0.15 dB and 92%, respectively, are achieved.

articleTitle: Measurement of beat length and perturbation length in long single-mode fibers by backscattered signal analysis
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We measured beat length and birefringence correlation length of several types of long single-mode fibers, using a new backscattering technique. Results represent the first experimental characterization of the random birefringence affecting long single-mode fibers.

articleTitle: Novel pumping schemes for thulium doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: With 1064 nm pumping, 5 dB extra gain is exhibited, and with a two-wavelengths pumping, 5 nm gain broadening and 16 nm gain shifting are experimentally shown for the thulium doped fluoride fiber amplifier.

articleTitle: The MONET project-a final report
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The MONET project ends in October 1999 with the completion and operation of a transparent, reconfigurable optical network in Washington, DC. This paper describes the network and summarizes experimental results, achieved in the first months of operation.

articleTitle: A novel optical label swapping technique using erasable optical single-sideband subcarrier label
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: To support optical multiprotocol label switching (MPLS) technology in an optical network, we have demonstrated subcarrier label swapping in a 96.2 km, three-node experiment, by using optical single-sideband modulation and an optical notch filter. At each intermediate switching node, an old subcarrier label can be suppressed by 25 dB, while the 2.5 Gb/s payload experienced only 2 dB loss.

articleTitle: Polarization properties of photonic bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the first analysis of polarization properties of photonic bandgap fibers. Strong birefringence may be obtained for modest non-uniformities in and around the core region, suggesting the use of photonic bandgap fibers as polarization maintaining components.

articleTitle: Chirp-free tunable PMD compensation using Hi-Bi nonlinearly-chirped FBGs in a dual-pass configuration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate chirp-free tunable PMD compensation for a l0 Gbit/s signal by using an adjustable high-birefringence nonlinearly-chirped FBG in a novel dual-pass configuration that significantly reduces the chirp induced by the FBG. We show PMD compensation with tunability from 250 to 600 ps in which the power penalty due to fiber dispersion in a 45 km link interacting with the FBG induced chirp is reduced from 4 to 0.5 dB.

articleTitle: Thermo-optically active polymeric photonic components
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on a variety of thermo-optically active polymeric components including tunable Bragg grating filters, tunable arrayed waveguide gratings, digital optical switches with low power consumption and high isolation, and variable optical attenuators with wide dynamic range.

articleTitle: Novel optical frequency discriminator with "perfect" linearity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: FM detection is possible with incoherent receivers and linear frequency filters. Our novel filter composed of dispersion compensation fiber gratings is compared to Mach Zehnder discriminators. Furthermore, this approach generalizes to arbitrary filter spectra.

articleTitle: Athermal and center wavelength adjustable arrayed-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Athermal and center wavelength adjustable AWGs with flat-top spectral responses are proposed. Low temperature sensitivity /spl sim/0.0013 nm//spl deg/C and precise center wavelength control less than 0.02 nm are demonstrated without additional loss and crosstalk penalty.

articleTitle: Measurement of the non-linear index of refraction, N/sub 2/, for various fiber types
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Using self-phase modulation, the nonlinear index of refraction for ten different types of optical fiber has been measured. It is found that the value of the index varies linearly with the power weighted germania concentration.

articleTitle: Evaluation of switching windows for fast optically-controlled SOA switches
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a novel algorithm to evaluate the performance of optical demultiplexers from standard switching-window measurements. Investigations of a SLALOM/TOAD demultiplexer for 80 Gb/s and 160 Gb/s show that biasing one arm of the interferometer by a constant phase offset significantly improves its performance.

articleTitle: Network application and system demonstration of WDM systems with very large spans (error-free 32/spl times/10 Gbit/s 750 km transmission over 3 amplified spans of 250 km)
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the network applications of WDM systems with very large spans. Enabling technologies are low loss fiber, large launch powers, Raman preamplification and forward error correction. An experiment using all these technologies is presented.

articleTitle: All-optical signal processing with photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical techniques for bit-level processing of high-speed signals will be reviewed, with emphasis on key device "building blocks" and on demonstrated and potential system applications, particularly optical signal regeneration.

articleTitle: Low-noise high gain dispersion compensating broadband Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Raman gain module compensating for both loss and dispersion of a 40 km standard telecommunication fiber span over the 1510-1565 nm band is reported. The optimized configuration ensures a low signal-spontaneous noise figure and negligible double Rayleigh scattering noise. The high gain margin of the amplifier makes it applicable for compensation of an 80 km span.

articleTitle: A flexible metro WDM ring using wavelength-independent subscriber equipment to share bandwidth
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Transparent optical networking has been proposed as a means for increasing capacity, improving performance, and decreasing costs, while simplifying network operations. For example, one facet of DARPA's next generation internet (NGI) initiative is focused on the development of transparent networks capable of handling IP traffic riding directly over WDM. We propose and demonstrate a transparent WDM metro ring architecture in which optics enables simultaneous provisioning of dedicated wavelengths for high-end users, while low-end users share wavelengths on "virtual rings". In both cases the customer's "end station" consists of low cost wavelength-independent components.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Statistical study of the influence of topology on wavelength usage in WDM networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a statistical study of wavelength usage in relation to topology characteristics for optical WDM networks. New general correlations between topology parameters and wavelength usage are identified to simplify the network planning process.

articleTitle: 10 simultaneously mode-locked and synchronized channels at 30 GHz from fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A laser source generating 10 synchronized wavelengths, mode-locked at 30 GHz and providing nearly 7 ps transform limited pulses across its output is presented. Mode-locking is achieved using an external 5 GHz optical pulse train.

articleTitle: Dispersion measurement using fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new dispersion measurement method is proposed, which gives the differential effective index of optical fiber in terms of optical wavelength by analyzing the transmission spectrum of a pair of cascaded long-period fiber gratings.

articleTitle: Spectrum-sliced bidirectional WDM PON
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a bidirectional wavelength-division-multiplexed (WDM) passive optical network (PON) based on spectrum-sliced technique. This network transmits fifteen 500 Mbps downstream and fifteen 155 Mbps upstream channels over single strand of conventional single-mode fiber.

articleTitle: Analysis on the network oscillations in the amplified WDM ring network-dependency on the channel power equalizer speed and network span length
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Chaotic lasing effect in a closed cycle in optically amplified ring network with channel power equalizers (CPE) has been simulated to reveal the dynamics of WDM ring network oscillation, WDM ring round-trip frequency, combined with the RC-time constant of channel power equaliser (CPE), determine oscillation behavior of the network.

articleTitle: Optical architecture for multi-terabit IP routers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel architecture is proposed for future multi-terabit Internet protocol routers, employing multiple cascaded stages of optical switching and buffering. External synchronisation is not required, and a void-filling algorithm simplifies hardware requirements.

articleTitle: Optical add/drop multiplexers based on X-crossing vertical coupler filters
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A simple OADM based on X-crossing InGaAsP-InP vertical coupler filters is demonstrated. Laterally separated input and output waveguides is achieved using a wafer bonding technique and double side wafer processing. Sidelobe level of /spl sim/26 dB and coupling efficiency of 97% are achieved for OADM with X-crossing angle of 0.25.

articleTitle: All-optical 3R regeneration and format conversion in an integrated SOA/DFB laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Simultaneous all-optical 3R regeneration and NRZ to RZ format conversion is demonstrated for the first time in an integrated SOA/DFB laser. After 10l km of standard fiber, a negative BER penalty of 1.5 dB is achieved after all-optical regeneration.

articleTitle: Demonstration of TMN management of a WDM network testbed
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have demonstrated configuration, fault protection, and performance management of a WDM network testbed. These experiments show the possibility to build a manageable client-independent optical transport layer, complying with current management standards.

articleTitle: Diamond-like film encapsulated fibers for long-length fiber grating production
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have developed a process to deposit a thin uniform layer of diamond-like film onto optical fibers. This UV-transparent film protects the fiber during the fiber grating inscription and maintains the geometry of the fiber so long length gratings can be fabricated.

articleTitle: Field trial of a European self-healing WDM optical network
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An optical self-healing WDM ring developed by Ericsson-the FlexingBus-has been successfully tested in a field trial in Telia's network in Stockholm, Sweden. The ring carried SDH, gigabit Ethernet, and digital video (CIR) traffic.

articleTitle: A new concept for the WDM module using a waveguide equipped with filter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report a directly deposited multilayer filter onto an end face of a polyimide waveguide. The hybrid integration of a waveguide equipped with filter and a silicon V-groove achieve the all-passive alignment process.

articleTitle: Nonlinear interaction of signal and noise in 10 Gb/s long distance RZ transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show that nonlinear coupling between signal and ASE noise in long-haul WDM dispersion-managed transmission is a significant impairment which limits the amount of accumulated dispersion that can be tolerated. A variety of dispersion compensation scenarios for a broad range of signal wavelengths is analyzed through computer simulations.

articleTitle: Diffusion processes in lightguide materials
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Diffusion of network forming and network modifying elements in silica were investigated. For boron, we found a linear relation between diffusion and viscosity. The diffusion coefficients of the rare earths and aluminum are closely related.

articleTitle: A novel bi-directional wavelength path switched ring (BWPSR): principle and experiment
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel bi-directional wavelength path switched ring (BWPSR) is proposed and demonstrated. Various optical channel layer protection schemes (1+1 VPSR, optical BLSR, and BWPSR) are discussed and compared. BER and jitter performances of BWPSR are measured. Interoperability and protection time are tested.

articleTitle: Micromachine-based fault-tolerant high resolution highspeed programmable fiber-optic attenuator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A programmable fiber-optic attenuator using a small tilt micromirror device is introduced, featuring digital control, alignment tolerance, and high speed, with a measured 37.8 dB optical attenuation and a 11-bit resolution.

articleTitle: Noise effects in polarization maintaining optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Excessive noise generation in optically amplified analog fiber optic systems due to different polarization-maintaining EDFA configurations is investigated. Increases in the effective RIN level of more than 20 dB are predicted and experimentally observed for double-pass configurations.

articleTitle: Parametric noise amplification near the zero-dispersion wavelength of optical fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We observe noise amplification induced by four-wave-mixing with two lasers having wavelengths symmetrically around the zero dispersion wavelength. Gain of /spl sim/lO dB is observed for 17 dBm laser power, within a /spl sim/25 nm.

articleTitle: Terabit field trial (100/spl times/10 Gb/s over a 4-span NDSF route)
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: MCIWORLDCOM and Nortel Networks have deployed a record capacity 1 terabit/s 4-span NDSF live traffic field trial. 100/spl times/10 Gb/s modulated channels, including fixed wavelength and tunable transmitters in the C- and L-bands, were multiplexed and amplified across 200 km, employing a state-of-the-art bi-directional interleaved architecture and L-band technology.

articleTitle: The impact of non-linear fiber effects on fiber choice for ultimate transmission capacity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Nonlinear effects in the transmission fiber, like self-phase modulation, cross-phase modulation, four-wave mixing, and stimulated Raman scattering will limit the ultimate capacity of long-haul WDM systems. We discuss the impact of the fiber characteristics on the ultimate limit and draw conclusions for the best choice of the transmission fiber.

articleTitle: Impact of pump and signal wavelength on inhomogeneous characteristics of L-band EDFAs
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Inhomogeneous gain saturation in C-band and L-band EDFAs is compared for the 980 nm and 1480 nm pump wavelength bands. Results demonstrate the manner in which pump wavelength and saturation signal wavelength affects the L-band inhomogeneous characteristic.

articleTitle: Novel wavelength-time spreading optical CDMA system using arrayed-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a novel two-dimensional code and transmitter/receiver structure using AWG for general multi wavelength-time optical CDMA network. We demonstrate via experiment that suggested scheme successfully performs encoding/decoding operations in addition to the possibility of incorporated dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication, and characterization of high-attenuation fibers with cladding mode suppression
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: High-attenuation fibers were developed with a special design to significantly reduce modal interference that occurs in short fiber lengths. A solution doping technique was used to introduce the transition elements into the core. The same degree of attentuation could be achieved at both 1310 and 1550 nm.

articleTitle: High power PM fiber amplifier and broadband source
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A polarization maintaining (PM) 1.5 /spl mu/m amplifier was demonstrated by externally inducing strain birefringence in a nominally non-polarization maintaining double cladding Er/Yb fiber. The 27 dBm amplifier had a 17 dB polarization extinction and was v-groove side-pumped by a broad stripe diode. A line broadband source is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Relaxed space switch crosstalk requirements: crosstalk analysis in the presence of laser wavelength referencing error and drift
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present for the first time analytical expressions characterizing homodyne beat noise effects in the presence of laser wavelength referencing error and drift, and show that for typical referencing error and drift values the crosstalk requirements for large space switches in optical cross-connects can be relaxed by up to fourteen decibels.

articleTitle: Wavelength reusability in wavelength-routed optical networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Wavelength reusability is proposed as an efficient criterion to evaluate the network performance in wavelength-routed optical networks. The maximum wavelength reusability is limited for a given network. The maximum wavelength reusability mainly depends on the average nodal degree.

articleTitle: Asymmetric probability density function of a signal with interferometric crosstalk in optically amplified systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An asymmetric probability density function (PDF) due to the beating of interferometric crosstalk and amplifier spontaneous emission (ASE) in a system with optical preamplifier was observed experimentally and explained theoretically. The theoretical PDF of the directly detected signal with one in-band incoherent interferer and ASE noise was compared with the experiment and is found to be in excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Retroreflector-based optical system for easily fabricable 2/spl times/2 micromechanical optical switch modules
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose the retroreflector-based optical system using the fiber collimator array, which extremely simplifies fabrication processed and offers low coupling loss of 0.29 dB. We also demonstrate 2/spl times/2 micromechanical optical switch module employing the optical system.

articleTitle: Fast and accurate determination of a tunable laser wavelength and its application to DWDM components
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We discuss the use of a tunable laser source with a built-in wavelength meter. The wavelength meter allows fast and accurate measurements of passive DWDM components with highest accuracy.

articleTitle: All-optical code conversion of 10 Gb/s BPSK codes without wavelength-shift by cross-phase modulation for optical code division multiplexing networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: All-optical code conversion of 10 Gb/s BPSK codes without wavelength-shift by use of cross-phase modulation in an optical fiber for optical code division multiplexing networks is proposed and experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: CATO: trans-layer dense wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM) network optimization. The clustering approach for large network design
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: DWDM network optimization and management problems include routing and wavelength assignment, protection switching, and resource allocation. A novel reduction technique in conjunction with a tested design tool, CATO, allows optimization of significantly larger networks.

articleTitle: Dynamic reconfiguration in WDM packet networks with wavelength limitations
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We develop load balancing algorithms for WDM packet networks that reduce network congestion by reconfiguring the logical topology. These algorithms use a simple iterative approach that minimizes network disruption and reduces electronic processing loads.

articleTitle: Spot-size-converter integrated ASM-LD's with 44.8 mA record low operation current at 85/spl deg/C
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A record low driving current of 44.8 mA for 10 mW output power at 85/spl deg/C was demonstrated for 1.3 /spl mu/m wavelength spot-size-converter integrated laser diodes by optimizing device parameters.

articleTitle: System impact of cascaded optical add/drop multiplexers based on tunable fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The system impact of cascaded wavelength routing nodes is investigated for a transparent all-optical network. A combination of simulations and experimental measurements is used to evaluate dynamic optical add/drop multiplexers based on tunable fiber gratings.

articleTitle: Dispersion-managed transmission of 100 Gb/s time-division-multiplexed return-to-zero format data
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of 100 Gb/s RZ TDM data over a 100 km link utilizing dense dispersion-management. Numerical simulations indicate transmission greater than 1000 km is possible.

articleTitle: Impact of electrostriction in single-channel 40 Gbit/s undersea systems in the presence of dispersion-management or optical 3R regeneration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate that electrostriction-induced interaction is responsible for limitations in 40 Gbit/s single-channel transmission systems performance even in presence of dispersion-management and that periodic optical 3R regeneration totally suppresses the phenomenon.

articleTitle: Outage due to polarization effects in a trans-oceanic system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We developed and validated a Stokes parameter model that was used to calculate the penalty due to polarization effects in a trans-oceanic system. We calculate the outage probability.

articleTitle: Temperature stability and mechanical strength of long-period fiber gratings fabricated with CO/sub 2/ laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We will present measurement results on two critical aspects of the reliability of long-period fiber gratings, temperature stability of the resonance peak shift and mechanical strength of the optical fiber with large residual mechanical stress.

articleTitle: Design parameters of dispersion decreasing fiber based OTDM source: quasi-adiabatic higher-order soliton compression from sinusoidal input signal
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a new scheme for generating a pedestal-free, femtosecond soliton pulse train by utilizing quasi-adiabatic high order soliton pulse evolution in dispersion decreasing fiber in conjunction with the intermediate pedestal suppression stage. A compression factor over 250 was achieved from 10 GHz sinusoidal input, to 207 fs soliton pulse train.

articleTitle: High density optical integration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: By proper design of optical waveguides and resonators with high index-contrast one may minimize the radiation loss. Such structures can be used to realize bends, waveguide crossings and filters of small size, leading to dense optical integration.

articleTitle: Colliding pulse mode locked laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The fabrication and performance of a colliding pulse mode locked laser is described. The laser has a threshold current of 5 mA and fiber coupled differential efficiency of 0.04 mW/mA. Mode locked pulses with /spl sim/1 ps width at /spl sim/10 GHz has been obtained.
