articleTitle: Transmission of 80/spl times/10 Gbit/s WDM channels with 50 GHz spacing over 500 km of LEAF/sup R/ fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of 80/spl times/10 Gbit/s channels over 5/spl times/100 km of LEAF fiber. The impact of optical nonlinearities for 50 GHz channel spacing is evaluated by comparing the results of different interleaved channel polarization experiments.

articleTitle: dBm output power from an engineered cladding-pumped Yb-free EDFA for L-band WDM applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have demonstrated a saturated output power of +26 dBm with a cladding-pumped Yb-free erbium-doped fiber amplifier owing to the matching of the multimode pumps wavelength with the erbium absorption spectrum. These results corresponded to saturated output powers of +23 dBm with a single multimode module and +26 dBm with two sources used in combination. Moreover, in the flat-gain regime, an output power of +24 dBm has been obtained for only 1.76 W launched pump power. Since the amplifier incorporated only packaged devices, this will make its gain flatness characteristics and high output powers available soon for the next generations of high bit-rate WDM systems.

articleTitle: 1.3 /spl mu/m vertical cavity amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report the first optically pumped 1.3 micron vertical cavity amplifier with a gain of 13.7 dB in reflection mode. Optimization of the output mirror reflectivity revealed a gain bandwidth of 31 GHz and a saturation power of /spl sim/5 dBm.

articleTitle: Impact of electrostriction in CATV networks' performance
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Electrostriction is identified as one of the main sources of crosstalk in CATV networks using WDM and sub-carrier multiplexing. The contribution of electrostriction to crosstalk is experimentally investigated for up to 8 WDM channels and enhancements of the overall crosstalk level of up to 5 dB are observed.

articleTitle: In-line gain control of the erbium doped fiber amplifier using samarium doped inner-cladding in the 1.5 /spl mu/m region
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new type of erbium doped fiber for optical amplifier was reported where erbium was doped in the center of the core and samarium doped in a ring in the cladding. By utilizing the spectral overlap of the absorption cross section of samarium in the inner-cladding and the emission cross section of erbium ion in the core, we demonstrated a new way of in-line control the gain spectrum of erbium doped amplifier pumped at 980 nm. The gain spectra in the conventional band were measured and we demonstrated potential of gain-flattening in the 1.5 mm region without external filters using the specially designed fiber. The effects of samarium doped inner-cladding on amplified spontaneous emission in the long band were also reported.

articleTitle: Upgrading and protecting traffic in an optical network by bottleneck-cut identification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An optical network can be cost-effectively upgraded by enhancing the capacity of links in the "bottleneck-cut". The "bottleneck-cut" information is also important for network protection. We develop and evaluate an algorithm for finding the "bottleneck-cut".

articleTitle: Cross-talk performance comparison among different OXC architectures
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Crosstalk performance of different OXC architectures are compared through simulations and preliminary experiments. We show that a careful OXC design can remove limitation due to imperfect switch (in experimentation a thermo-optical element) operation.

articleTitle: A very low failure rate of COD free high power 0.98 /spl mu/m laser diode with the window structure
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A very low failure rate of a 0.98 /spl mu/m laser diode is reported. COD free characteristics is realized. The cumulative failure rate 0.4% for wear-out and 5.6% for sudden failure is estimated 25 years later at 25 C-250 mW.

articleTitle: 1.28 Tbit/s throughput 8/spl times/8 optical switch based on arrays of gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifier gates
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report here, to our knowledge, on the first demonstration of a modular 8/spl times/8 optical switch built with opto-hybrid 8/spl times/1 SOA-based space switch modules. A WDM experiment shows that this 8 x 8 optical switch offers a potential of 1.28 Tbit/s throughput.

articleTitle: 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength-selectable microarray DFB-LDs with integrated MMI combiner, SOA, and EA-modulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We developed compact (1.136 mm/sup 2/) eight-channel wavelength selectable microarray DFB-LDs with monolithically integrated 8/spl times/1 MMI combiner, S0A, and EA-modulator. The wavelength tuning range of 15.3 nm with uniform device characteristics and 2.5 Gbit/s modulation performance were successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Efficient architecture for a duplex multi-stage optical non-blocking switch
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a novel architecture for an optical cross-connect based on full duplex switches that support reciprocal traffic. The architecture is based on a Clos switch and is proven to be non-blocking. The number of basic devices needed for it is about half the number needed in a conventional one-way architecture.

articleTitle: Dispersion slope compensating fibers for L-band WDM systems using NZ-DSF
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Dispersion slope compensating fiber, which upgrades installed NZ-DSF to l-band D-WDM transmission line, was designed and fabricated. Both polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) and bending loss are low enough for moduling. It can compensate the dispersion of +NZ-DSF transmission line within /spl plusmn/0.3ps/nm/km over 1580-1620 nm.

articleTitle: Effects of unisolated optical sources on bidirectional SCM transmission systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on the performances of the bidirectional subcarrier-multiplexed transmission systems using unisolated optical sources. In particular, we have identified the dominant mechanisms of performance degradations for various system configurations using unisolated Fabry-Perot lasers or LED's.

articleTitle: Fiber pigtail detachable plastic MiniDIL transmitter with a tool-free optical connector
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A fiber-pigtail-detached plastic MiniDIL transmitter module that has a tool-free optical connector and meets the OC 3 and OC 12 has been developed to enable low-cost fabrication. The optical connector can be connected and disconnected from the module without any specific tool. Fiber output of more that 0.4 mW, insertion loss of less than 0.3 dB, return loss of more than 42 dB, and repeatability of more than 30 times were achieved.

articleTitle: Optical frequency mixers for WDM and TDM applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: All-optical wavelength conversion for WDM, gated mixing for TDM, and spectral inversion for dispersion correction have been demonstrated in simple three-wave mixing and in cascade mixing devices. Low conversion loss (3 dB) and wide bandwidths (70 nm) can be obtained with moderate pump powers (tens of mW).

articleTitle: All-optical storage of picosecond pulse packets using wavelength-induced XPM and parametric amplification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present phase-insensitive loading of external data in an all-optical storage line wherein linear loss is compensated by phase-sensitive parametric amplification. Storage is achieved for about 100 circulations within the fiber buffer.

articleTitle: Influence of RZ and NRZ signal format on the high-speed performance of gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: High-speed experiments show that the influence from the limited relaxation frequency of GC-SOAs that severely degrades the performance for NRZ signals is reduced by using RZ signals, thus resulting in a higher input power dynamic range.

articleTitle: Photosensitivity in tin-doped silica optical fibres
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Permanent gratings (refractive index modulation /spl sim/3/spl middot/10/sup 4/) were written in tin-doped silica optical fibres with low levels of SnO/sub 2/ (/spl sim/0.15 mol%). In Ge-doped silica, /spl sim/10 mol% GeO/sub 2/ is required to produce a comparable result under similar conditions.

articleTitle: Design of a Pan-European lightwave core and access networking trial (ACTS-PELICAN project)
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The PELICAN project aims at the field demonstration of a large managed optical network, featuring 3 network partitions with different topologies, various types of network elements and supervision schemes. New network functions, management and protections are implemented.

articleTitle: Recovered efficiency of optical regeneration control on dispersion-managed solitons : analysis and application to a 32/spl times/40 Gbit/s transoceanic system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate that a local conversion from dispersion-managed soliton to nonlinear Schrodinger soliton restores the efficiency of optical regeneration control and enables the transmission of 32/spl times/40 Gbit/s over transoceanic distances with high spectral efficiency (1.4 nm channel spacing).

articleTitle: Performance comparison between SCDCF-based system and RDF-based system in slope-compensating transoceanic WDM transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Transmission performance of single mode fibre (SMF)-based dispersion flattened systems using slope compensating dispersion compensated fibre (SCDCF) and reverse dispersion fibre (RDF) was experimentally investigated. The feasibility of transmission distance enhancement in 340 Gbit/s (32/spl times/10.66 Gbits) WDM transmission was confirmed with the proper dispersion map.

articleTitle: Simultaneous bi-directional of C- and L-band erbium doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel wideband amplifier using a single laser diode is demonstrated. Simultaneous bi-directional amplification of conventional and long-band signals is achieved with utilization of unwanted amplified spontaneous pump for the long-band section.

articleTitle: Wavelength tuning range enhanced single resonant band fiber filter using a long period grating (LPG) with ultra thin cladding layer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A unique fiber filter using a LPG with ultra thin cladding layer (/spl sim/32 /spl mu/m) is presented, which has a single resonant band within 1000 nm to 1700 nm wavelength tuning sensitivity as large as 30 nm shift for a 2/spl times/1O-3 surrounding refractive index change.

articleTitle: High-speed WDM transmission using highly dispersed pulses
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Two channel transmission at 40 Gb/s is demonstrated over 800 km of conventional fiber, using 2.5 to 3.7 ps pulses for RZ format to minimize nonlinear effects and enable localized dispersion compensation. Channel separations as close as 1.8 nm are possible, for spectral efficiency of 18%.

articleTitle: SRS crosstalk in preemphasized WDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: With a new simple model for stimulated Raman scattering crosstalk and an 30 dBm system experiment we found that the shortest and longest wavelength channels are affected most by SRS crosstalk independent of the preemphasis.

articleTitle: Novel temperature insensitive long-period grating by using the refractive index of the outer cladding
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show the temperature sensitivity of long period gratings (LPGs) in fibre can be completely eliminated by using the outer cladding index. Blue shift of LPG combined with a red shift caused by the recoating led to a temperature sensitivity of 0.07 nm/100/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Picosecond pulse-duration-selectable soliton source based upon adiabatic compression in a Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Raman amplification of 10 ps soliton pulses generated directly from an electroabsorption modulator based source have been adiabatically compressed in a Raman fibre amplifier, giving a pulse duration tunable source, 1-10 ps at 10 GHz and average powers up to 650 mW dependent on the magnitude of the amplification.

articleTitle: Dispersion-induced power penalty in fiber-Bragg-grating WDM filter cascades
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: In wavelength-division-multiplexed optical networks signals pass through cascades of multiplexing/demultiplexing filters. We present experimental measurements and theoretical modeling of transmission power penalty at 10 Gbps due to dispersion slope of fiber-Bragg-grating and thin-film cascades.

articleTitle: Erbium-doped planar waveguide amplifiers integrated with silica waveguide technology
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Summary form only given. We addressed the main challenges of integration of high refractive index Er-doped aluminosilicate waveguides with silicon optical bench technology. Performance of waveguide amplifiers integrated with pump/signal WDM will be presented, and issues related to their integration will be discussed.

articleTitle: Grating spectra in air-silica microstructure fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report detailed spectral characterization of optical gratings written in different air-silica microstructured optical fibers. Our data reveal the propagation of higher order leaky modes in fibers with periodically spaced air-holes (photonic crystal fibers). As the air-hole diameter increases (i.e., mode ceases to penetrate the inner holes) spectra reveal cladding modes defined by the inner cladding only.

articleTitle: Four-wave mixing in EDFAs
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We study FWM in C- and L-band EDFAs. We observe that FWM efficiency is determined by fiber length and channel spacing. We show that FWM from EDFAs exceeds that from non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber in DWDM system.

articleTitle: Multiple carrier analog transmission system with Er/sup 3+/ doped planar optical waveguide amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report for the first time the use of two types of Er/sup 3+/ planar optical waveguide amplifiers in 77 channel CATV fiber links. Single and novel composite amplifiers in the headend and in cascade allow high quality broadcast transmission in terms of CNR, CTB and CSO over 52 km of standard allwave/sup TM/ fiber.

articleTitle: Dynamic-gain-tilt-free long-wavelength band erbium doped fiber amplifiers utilizing temperature dependent characteristics of gain spectrum
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: By a novel automatic level control technique the thermal behavior of an EDF and the dynamic-gain-tilt of the long-wavelength band EDFA have been successfully reduced to less than O.15 dB over a 4 dB input power range.

articleTitle: Analysis of synchronous intensity modulation control of 40 Gbit/s dispersion-managed soliton transmissions
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Transmission control of dispersion-managed solitons by means of in-line synchronous intensity modulators and no filtering is analyzed. The feasibility of a 40 Gbit/s dispersion-managed transmission over 20 Mm regenerated only intensity modulation is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Hybrid thin film WDM and optical switch devices for optical add/drop
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We compare the use of integrated hybrid switch/WDM components as compared to discrete components for switched OADM systems. System issues such as loss balancing, ripple accumulation, and bandwidth narrowing are also discussed.

articleTitle: Optical layer protection of ATM traffics using a novel 4-fiber WDM ring with an ability to carry extra traffic
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: ATM/IP over WDM ring with optical layer protection is proposed and demonstrated. Traffics are 1+1 protected ATM OC-48c and a low priority part-time IP traffic. A very fast protection time is experimentally verified by both physical layer and ATM layer test results.

articleTitle: Error-free transmission of image fiber-optic 2D parallel interconnection using VCSEL/PD arrays: experiment
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: 8/spl times/8 2-D VCSEL/PD arrays were interconnected by an image fiber for the first time. Optical alignment was achieved without power-monitoring. The crosstalk was /spl sim/34 dB and the misalignment tolerance for a BER of 10/sup -9/ was 85 /spl mu/m and the evaluated total throughput is 2.25 Tbps.

articleTitle: Low-loss and flat pass-band 1/spl times/8 arrayed-waveguide grating multi/demultiplexers with athermal spectrum for metropolitan area networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We successfully developed a low-loss and flat pass-band 1/spl times/8 arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) multi/demultiplexer module with an athermal spectrum. The insertion loss was only 3.8 dB which is 40% lower than that of previous AWGs.

articleTitle: A line coding scheme for reducing timing jitter in WDM soliton systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose the fragmentation code (FC), designed by exploiting the nature of collision induced timing jitter (CITJ) in WDM soliton systems. We show by simulations, that the FC on effectively reduce bit errors due to CITJ.

articleTitle: 5 Gbit/s transmission through an all-fiber-optic add/drop device based on a microsphere whispering-gallery-resonance system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: 15 GHz bandwidth and 23 dB extinction ratio have been realized for a taper-resonator-taper add/drop device. The BER performance of the system has shown only 1 dB penalty at 5 Gbit/s and no signs of an error floor.

articleTitle: Dispersion maps with optimized amplifier placement for wavelength-division-multiplexing
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We analyze amplifier placement in a two-step dispersion map and determine configurations that simultaneously minimize dispersive radiation in multiple channels for wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM). Numerical simulations are performed to verify the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Over half-Watt output power 1.48 /spl mu/m wavelength EDFA pumping ASM LD's
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A record high CW output power of 504 mW with a single-lateral-mode was achieved by optimizing the cavity length and the front facet reflectivity. A module with up to 337 mW fiber-coupled CW output power was attained.

articleTitle: Tunable compensation of the dispersion slope mismatch in dispersion-managed systems using a sampled nonlinearly-chirped FBG
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate tunable dispersion slope compensation for three 10 Gbit/s WDM channels using a sampled nonlinearly-chirped FBG. The replicated sampled-FBG wavelength bands have a different separation than the WDM channels, causing each channel to experience a different dispersion compensation that can be tuned upon stretching of the FBG. We achieve significant power penalty reduction using our tunable dispersion-slope-compensation method over 900 and 1200 km fiber links.

articleTitle: On prioritization and optimal buffer management in photonic packet switching nodes
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The effects of prioritization and buffer sharing for packet switching are analyzed analytically. An adaptive methodology is proposed and evaluated for maximizing switch throughput by optimally managing the usually restricted buffer depth of photonic nodes.

articleTitle: Pulse chirp control in an actively mode-locked fiber laser using a dual-drive variable-chirp modulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that the chirp imposed on the pulses from an actively mode-locked erbium fiber ring laser can be controlled by using a dual-drive variable-chirp modulator as mode locker.

articleTitle: Dual-band hybrid transmission line consisting of pure silica core fiber and dispersion compensating fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Ultimately small dispersion slope less than 0.003 ps/nm2/km was realized for both c and l bands by a novel pure-silica core fiber/dispersion compensating fiber hybrid transmission line, which also exhibited small average attenuation of 0.205 dB/km and low non-linearity.

articleTitle: Fiber-based metropolitan access networks for Internet traffic
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: While fiber optics has made the Internet what it is today, more advanced uses of fiber such as local access networks must deal with some of the challenging characteristics of Internet traffic.

articleTitle: All-optical 2R-regeneration of 10 Gbit/s RZ data transmitted over 30000 km in a dispersion-managed system using an electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: All-optical 2R regeneration of 10 Gbit/s RZ data transmitted over 30000 km in a dispersion-managed system was demonstrated using an electroabsorption modulator at the receiver. The modulator suppresses the accumulated optical noise, improving the signal-to-noise ratio of the transmitted data.

articleTitle: Photonic 100 Gb/s serial-to-parallel converter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate full demultiplexing of a single 100 Gb/s time division multiplexed optical data stream into eight parallel 12.5 Gb/s streams. The device is based on lithium niobate intensity modulators and requires no nonlinear optical elements.

articleTitle: 10 Gbit/s/spl times/4 ch WDM upgrading system on an installed optical amplifier submarine system designed for single-wavelength channel transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We describe the design concepts and performance of a commercially available 10 Gbit/s/spl times/4 ch WDM system applied for an installed fiber submarine system originally designed for single wavelength channel transmission.

articleTitle: Automatic absolute frequency calibration of tunable optical sources
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a procedure that can be used to automatically calibrate the optical frequency of DFB MQW tunable semiconductor laser optical sources by measuring and recognizing the absorption pattern of a reference optical filter such as a gas cell.

articleTitle: A geometrical model of polarization mode dispersion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A geometrical model of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) develops the PMD dynamical equations from first principles instead of phenomenologically and is extensible to polarization dependent loss. The utility of the geometrical approach is demonstrated by analyzing a fiber model with retarder plates forming a Markov process.

articleTitle: 1.6 Tb/s (40/spl times/40 Gb/s) total capacity 4-node optical networking with fully programmable A/D devices
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 4-node dynamically reconfigurable optical network, using integrated add/drop devices, is demonstrated. Aggregate capacity of 1.6 Tb/s (40/spl times/40 Gb/s), spectral efficiency of 0.4 bits/s/Hz, Q values larger than 18 dB and wide tolerance to wavelength misalignment are key results.

articleTitle: 30 Gbps, broadly tunable, all-optical, clock recovery circuit
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical clock recovery is demonstrated up to 30 Gbps, with very low modulation pattern even for long series of consecutive 0's. The circuit uses all-optical gain modulation of a SOA in a fiber ring laser.

articleTitle: Equalization of the non-flat erbium gain spectrum using the multiport lattice filter model
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose an accurate modeling technique of long period fiber gratings. The proposed technique is, then applied to synthesize long period fiber gratings for the erbium gain equalization using simulated annealing and steepest descent methods.

articleTitle: 10-Gbit/s RZ pulses using an all-silicon nonlinear transmission line integrated circuit
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate 25 ps wide electrical pulses using a nonlinear transmission line (NLTL) integrated circuit fabricated on high-resistivity silicon. These pulses are modulated electrically and used to drive a LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder modulator to create optical 10 Gbit/s RZ data with 27 ps pulse width.

articleTitle: 80 Gbit/s optical clock recovery using an electrical phase locked loop, and commercially available components
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Polarisation and wavelength insensitive 80 Gbit/s optical clock recovery using an electrical phase locked loop entirely comprising commercially available components is demonstrated. The system exhibited excellent long-term stability, with a timing jitter of /spl sim/250 fs.

articleTitle: Ultra-low phonon energy glasses for the high-performance 1.3 /spl mu/m-window amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Emission properties of 1.3 /spl mu/m fluorescence from Pr/sup 3+/ or Dy/sup 3+/ were investigated using host glasses with ultra-low phonon energy. Highly efficient 1.3 /spl mu/m amplifier materials can be realized from selenide and GeGaS-CsBr glasses.

articleTitle: Novel properties of air-silica microstructure optical fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Microstructure air-silica optical fibers with anomalous group-velocity dispersion at visible wavelengths are demonstrated. The linear and nonlinear optical properties of these structures are examined and their potential applications discussed.

articleTitle: Crosstalk caused by non-ideal output filters in CATV/WDM lightwave systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Experimental and analytic results show that imperfections in the output demultiplexer of a WDM system cause significant crosstalk between WDM channels. Pass band flatness, polarization-dependent loss, and channel isolation are critical, and currently are not specified adequately for high-capacity digital CATV systems.

articleTitle: Low-crosstalk, loss and PDL grating demultiplexer for application in terabit WDM routed networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on the performance of a diffraction grating demultiplexer for narrow channel spacings of /spl les/50 GHz (/spl les/0.4 nm). The device exhibited a fiber-to-fiber loss of 3.8 dB, very low adjacent channel crosstalk of -43 dB, background crosstalk of -55 dB and polarization dependence of <0.3 dB. The transmission performance with 16/spl times/10 Gbit/s channels is also reported.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable all-optical networking at terabit transmission rates
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on a transparent metropolitan fiber-ring composed of reconfigurable OADMs. Wavelength channel routing by tunable fiber Bragg-gratings and optical switching matrices is investigated. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the high capacity WDM-ring within the KOMNET field-trial.

articleTitle: 32/spl times/10 Gbit/s transmission over 8000 km using hybrid Raman-erbium doped fiber optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 32/spl times/10 Gbit/s transmission experiment over 8000 km has been carried out using hybrid optical amplifiers composed of Raman and erbium doped fiber amplifiers. Active gain equalization based on amplification has been also demonstrated.

articleTitle: All-optical laser synchronization and clock recovery based on dynamic parametric gain modulation
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel all-optical scheme for laser synchronization and clock recovery is demonstrated by combining the parametric gain modulation in a pulse-pumped nonlinear loop mirror with soliton shaping in a nonlinear amplifying loop mirror.

articleTitle: Upgrade capacity of 10 Gb/s WDM systems employing negative non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate that by strategic selection of channel plan and power levels, a 400 milometer 10 Gigabit per second system over a negative non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber (Corning SMF-LS) may operate with 38 channels over a 32 nanometer band close to lambda zero.

articleTitle: 1T bit/s(100 ch/spl times/10 G bit/s) WDM repeaterless transmission over 200 km with Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have demonstrated a record-breaking capacity repeaterless transmission experiment. 1T bit/s transmission over 200 km was achieved with densely WDM signals and Raman amplification.

articleTitle: Corrugated long period fiber gratings as band-rejection filters
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a new band-rejection filter made of a corrugated long period fiber grating whose transmission loss and wavelength can be tuned more than 25 dB and 40 nm by applying different amounts of strains and twisting angles.

articleTitle: Testing optical time-division multiplexed transmission systems with interleaved bit sequences
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We compare experimentally the performance of a 10 Gb/s channel encoded with a pseudo-random bit sequence and with interleaved bit sequences typical of OTDM experiments. For linear transmission conditions IBS patterns are found to yield slightly worse performances.

articleTitle: 740 km transmission of 78-channel 64-QAM signals (2.34 Gb/s) without dispersion compensation by using a recirculating loop
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A long distance 1550 nm subcarrier multiplexed lightwave trunk system which transported 78 channels of 64-QAM signal was demonstrated in a recirculating loop experiment. Each channel can achieve a carrier-to-( noise + nonlinear distortion) ratio of 30 dB after 740 km transmission through conventional single-mode fiber without dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of new regeneration scheme for 40 Gbit/s dispersion-managed long-haul transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We experimentally show, for the first time, that optical 3R-regeneration by synchronous modulation can be efficiently implemented in dispersion-managed transmission. Successful association of both techniques is demonstrated at 4O Gbit/s over more than 10000 km.

articleTitle: All-optical output-port contention resolution using subcarrier-multiplexing
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate an all-optical contention resolution technique that preserves the wavelength of two same-wavelength contending incoming 2.5 Gbit/s channels. This is achieved by optically subcarrier-multiplexing one channel to a higher RF frequency beyond the first baseband channel on the same input wavelength. By using narrow (/spl sim/5 GHz) fiber Fabry-Perot filters for demultiplexing we recovered each channel using a baseband receiver with <1 dB power penalty.

articleTitle: Sprint perspective on next generation multi-service transport and switching networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: I describe the evolving transmission and switching technology, services and performance requirements and discusses factors influencing the deployment of next generation systems. The significant distinctions between metropolitan and long-haul applications are also presented.

articleTitle: Reduction of crosstalk in semiconductor optical amplifiers by amplifying dispersed WDM signals (7/spl times/20 Gb/s)
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The dynamic range of semiconductor optical amplifiers is increased considerably at high bit rates by amplifying dispersed WDM signals. We demonstrate a fivefold increase in the dynamic range in a WDM experiment at channel rates of 20 Gbit/s (7/spl times/20 Gbit/s).

articleTitle: Compact tunable polymer WDM devices for on-chip integration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper discusses the fabrication and optical properties of polymer-based arrayed waveguide gratings and assesses the potential for optoelectronic integration with on-chip photodetectors. The work is carried out using a planar waveguide based on AlliedSignal polymer materials.

articleTitle: Narrow-bandwidth tunable Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide filter with cascaded Fabry-Perot structure
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Broadcasting stations require tunable optical filters with a narrow bandwidth in order to increase the capacity of their video-routing networks. A cascaded Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide filter composed of two Fabry-Perot filters has been designed for 128-channel 12.5 GHz-spaced dense-wavelength-division-multiplexing.

articleTitle: Simultaneous spectral filtering and wavelength monitoring of a DWDM transmitter using a tunable Fabry-Perot filter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: For a cost-effective realization of a DWDM transmitter, a temperature-tunable silicon chip Fabry-Perot filter has been applied. It allows simultaneous reduction of dispersion effects and real-time wavelength monitoring of the directly modulated laser.

articleTitle: Unrepeatered 80 Gbit/s RZ single channel transmission over 160 km of standard fiber at 1.55 /spl mu/m with a large wavelength tolerance
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Unrepeatered 80 Gbit/s RZ single channel transmission over 160 km of standard single-mode fiber at 1.55 /spl mu/m is reported using passive compensation of dispersion and dispersion-slope. Error-free transmission (BER=10-9) with a receiver sensitivity of -22 dBm wavelength tolerance of 10 nm was achieved.

articleTitle: High speed integrated acousto-optic switch with high extinction ratio
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The technology of single phase unidirectional transducer and focused transducer was adopted for the design of acousto-optic switch. The extinction ratio up to 32 dB and switching speed at 300 ns was achieved.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of MAC protocol for SuperPON using WDM
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We design MAC protocols for two different SuperPON upgrading architectures using WDM which are considered as future broadband access network. Both protocols are based on the dynamic slot allocation in order to maximize the multiplexing gain of upstream band-width. Two different WDM-PON architectures are compared in a view of MAC performance. According to simulation, we can know that architecture-1 (in which wavelength multiplexers are placed at amplified splitter) utilizes upstream bandwidth more flexibly than architecture-2 because it shows stable distribution of transfer delay and less CDV regardless of offered load.

articleTitle: Cascadability improvement of a cross-gain modulation wavelength converter using a grating based optical add/drop multiplexer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: By adding a grating based optical add/drop multiplexer, the maximum cascaded number of a cross-gain modulation based wavelength converter is improved from two to six rounds in a loop experiment at 10 Gb/s due to the improved high frequency response of the converter.

articleTitle: Dynamic performance evaluation in a WDM trunk and branch network incorporating 1:N wavelength protection
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a theoretical study on the dynamic performance requirements for the successful application of a proposed 1 for N wavelength protection scheme to wavelength routed trunk and branch type optical networks.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gbit/s error-floor free transmission with high extinction ratio using directly modulated 1.55 /spl mu/m tapered lasers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The emergence of a BER floor using a directly modulated laser is studied versus the modulation extinction ratio. A selection on efficiency leads to a 100% DFB yield for floor-free transmission at a high extinction ratio of 14 dB.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion in optical communication systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)

articleTitle: Generation of 1O GHz pulse packets from an actively mode-locked fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A method to generate packets of short (10 ps) high quality pulses directly from an actively mode-locked fiber ring laser at 10 GHz is demonstrated by locking the packet repetition frequency to the fundamental laser cavity frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of evolution of over-modulated supervisory data in a cascade of all-optical wavelength converters
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We analyze the evolution of sub-carrier modulated supervisory data crossing a cascade of all-optical wavelength converters. Mixing between these data and the high-bit-rate signal has been identified to be of significant consequences.

articleTitle: An integrable and cost effective FTTH-network structure
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Integrability installation expenses, network capacity and the possibility for future upgrading are compared for alternative fiber-to-the-home-network structures. The most effective structure is a passive, along-the-route-branched two-fiber-ribbon network suitable for time domain multiplexed transmission.

articleTitle: All-optical remote location of high polarization mode dispersion fiber spans using stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report an all-optical remote locator of high PMD fiber spans using stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS). Both the length of the high PMD fiber span and the magnitude of PMD itself can be inferred from the slope change of the reflected SBS pulse.

articleTitle: Multisolitons in dispersion management with fibre Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have studied the propagation of prechirped pulse groups in a fibre Bragg grating dispersion-managed system. We have discovered stable multisoliton solutions with fixed values for the phase difference and distance between adjacent pulses. These solutions may propagate for very long distances with the ultimate limitation of noise amplification.

articleTitle: 'Phase portraits' for characterizing advanced lasers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show that plotting the instantaneous optical frequency against power gives an instantly recognizable and useful fingerprint of the dynamic operation of lasers. We show simulated examples of bulk, MQW, unstable and tunable lasers.

articleTitle: Reference configuration for performance management in multiwavelength optical transport networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A set of reference points for performance management is proposed, which is based on the general functional architecture of the multiwavelength optical transport networks. These reference points can be mapped into the physical interfaces of optical networks to guide the execution of performance monitoring and controlling.

articleTitle: A low-cost compact multimode/singlemode WWDM transceiver module for 10 Gb/s applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Data communications, telecommunications, and computer interconnects are converging on the need for a very low cost 10 Gb/s interconnect. We present results on a long-wavelength wide-wavelength-division multiplexed transceiver module for both multimode and singlemode applications.

articleTitle: Code-division-multiplexing-compatible coding and decoding of directly driven DFB laser bit streams
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical implementation of code-multiplexing is heavily contingent upon compatibility of encoding devices with standard laser sources. We demonstrate encoding and decoding of RZ signals generated at 2.5 Gbps by direct-driving of a semiconductor DFB laser.

articleTitle: Cross-phase modulation in multiple-wavelength adiabatic soliton repeaterless transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate four-channel, wavelength-division-multiplexed transmission over 235 km using adiabatic soliton propagation. Adiabatic evolution of the spectrum allows precise characterization of soliton cross-phase modulation effects.

articleTitle: Frequency, mode and power stabilization of a widely tunable SSG-DBR laser at 40 ITU channels
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A feedback control circuit is demonstrated for a widely tunable SSG-DBR laser. It monitors active section voltage to maintain mode stability, and uses a Fabry-Perot etalon as reference to lock the laser frequency to a specific ITU channel with better than 1.0 GHz accuracy.

articleTitle: 10/spl times/10 Gb/s cross-phase modulation suppressor using WDM narrowband fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a 10/spl times/10 Gb/s cross-phase modulation suppressor based on series of WDM narrowband fiber Bragg gratings. When inserted 10/sup -7/ error floors are turned into a low 1 dB penalty after transmission over 5/spl times/100 km NZDSF.

articleTitle: Effects of stimulated Raman scattering on pilot-tone based WDM supervisory technique
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on the effects of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) on the pilot-tone based WDM monitoring technique. We measured the SRS-induced ghost ones after compensating the effects of EDFA's slow gain dynamics. Using these results, we estimated the maximum size of WDM network that the pilot-tone based monitoring technique could support.

articleTitle: A novel active holographic arrayed-waveguide grating for WDM subsystems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We describe simulation results of a novel active AWG indicating optical add/drop multiplexing with passband-flattened channels and suppressions of 15 dB and EDFA gain equalisation with a dynamic range of 12 dB, based on holographic Fourier techniques.

articleTitle: Bi-directional, polarization-independent four-wave mixing in semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Polarization-independent four-wave mixing is obtained in semiconductor optical amplifiers by splitting the incoming fields with a polarization beam splitter and injecting the resulting counter-propagating beam in the amplifier.

articleTitle: Design of thin-film interference filters for telecommunications applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Designs for the following types of filters will be discussed: edge filters for separating the 1310 nm and 1550 nm bands, ultra-narrowband 10 GHz filters for DWDM and filters for equalizing the gain of erbium-doped fibers.

articleTitle: Flexibly variable spectrum equalizer for spectral tilt compensation
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new variable-spectrum-equalizer (VSEQ) which combines the polarization dependence of dielectric film with magneto-optics is proposed and demonstrated. The VSEQ features flexible equalization capability with a simple drive-circuit maintaining wide dynamic-range (7 dB) and wide bandwidth (35 nm).

articleTitle: High-speed optical devices for 40 Gbit/s optical receivers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper reviews recent progress in wide-band photoreceiver OEICs composed of a waveguide pin photodiode and a HEMT distributed amplifier and high-output photodiodes called uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes in which only electrons act as carriers.

articleTitle: Actively Q-switched all-fiber laser with a fiber Bragg grating of variable reflectivity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A Q-switched fiber laser using an acoustically modulated fiber grating was implemented for producing 1550.5 nm pulses of 7.6 /spl mu/J in pulse energy, 150 nsec in pulse width, and 5 kHz in repetition frequency.

articleTitle: New possibilities with holey fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Holey fiber technology offers the potential for the development of fibers with unique optical properties including unusual and useful dispersion and nonlinear characteristics. We explore the design possibilities and suggest potential applications of the technology.

articleTitle: A 10 Gbit/s, 160 Gchip/s OCDMA coding:decoding system based on superstructured fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present results on upgrading the superstructure grating approach to both far higher data rates (10 Gb/s), far shorter chip-lengths (6.4 ps) and far higher grating reflectivities (up to 50%) than previously demonstrated. We demonstrate the flexibility and precision of our continuous scanning fiber/phase mask technique by fabricating both unipolar and bipolar coding and decoding gratings with close to the theoretically designed spectral response, and time domain performance characteristics. We present the results of BER measurements at 10 Gbit/s on a decoded pulse sequence both before and after transmission through 25km of standard fiber which show there to be no noise-penalty associated with either the coding:decoding process, or the transmission of the coded pulse itself.

articleTitle: Transmission trials of perfluorinated GI-POF
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Gbps transmission trials of PFGI-POF which has low loss and high bandwidth were successfully performed and the transmission system with commercially available transceivers and switches were confirmed. PFGI-POF duplex cable was applied to the part of LAN system as a demonstration which is working in the labs. We proved the systems high speed transmission capability.

articleTitle: Dynamic routing in the crosstalk reduced optical add/drop multiplexer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new configuration of optical add/drop multiplexer supporting channel bypass and add/drop is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The scheme allows double passing in the grating based Mach-Zehnder interferometer, resulting an improved rejection of homodyne crosstalk.

articleTitle: Wideband multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Simultaneous lasing of stable 34 lines with /spl sim/100 GHz channel spacing in 1535-1562 nm range is demonstrated from a frequency shifted feedback type multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber ring laser including a gain flattening filter.

articleTitle: Re-configurable 1:N protection system in an optical cross-connect network using branch state of a LiNbO/sub 3/ optical switch
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate an optical reconfigurable 1:N protection system which uses the branch state of LiNbO/sub 3/ optical switches and results in high availability of a spare route in the network. Reliable operations on restoration and re-configuration for a 10 Gb/s signal are confirmed.

articleTitle: Crosstalk reduction of arrayed waveguide gratings by UV trimming of individual waveguides without H/sub 2/-loading
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Fabrication induced phase errors of arrayed waveguide gratings have been reduced using UV-trimming of grating waveguides. Phase error compensation up to 5 rad and crosstalk reduction down to /spl sim/35 dB have been achieved without hydrogen loading.

articleTitle: Highly nonlinear chalcogenide glasses for ultrafast all optical switching in optical TDM communication systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Single-mode planar waveguides were fabricated from chalcogenide glass compounds with large Kerr nonlinearities. Strong self-phase modulation of sub-ps pulses along with low linear and nonlinear absorption losses demonstrates the potential for integrated all-optical switching applications.

articleTitle: Guided longitudinal acoustic modes in spontaneous and stimulated Brillouin scattering in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate the Brillouin gain spectrum in the spontaneous and stimulated regimes in AllWave/sup TM/, TrueWave/sup TM/ and dispersion compensating fibers. It is found that several longitudinal modes, depending on the core diameters, exist in the spontaneous regime but decay as the process becomes stimulated. Also, our results on the linewidth narrowing are in an agreement with the theory in undepleted-pump regime.

articleTitle: Distance-independent RF fading compensation using a tunable nonlinearly-chirped FBG in a phase diversity configuration
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We use a nonlinearly-chirped fibre Bragg grating (FBG) in a phase diversity configuration to achieve distance-independent RF power fading compensation for double sideband (DSB) subcarrier-multiplexed systems. We demonstrate compensation for RF power fading from 0 to 150 km for 8, 10 and 12 GHz, with received RF power in all cases flat to within 1 dB.

articleTitle: Performance of self-injection locked fiber Fabry-Perot laser with short feedback cavity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Single-frequency and single-polarization lasing can be generated in a compact self-injection locked fiber Fabry Perot laser with a short fiber Bragg grating feedback cavity without any discrete polarization control components. A 10 Gb/s NRZ transmission test demonstrates the laser's fiber communications.

articleTitle: Optical backplanes
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper discusses short-distance optical interconnects for distributed digital systems. We describe two-dimensional parallel optical interconnect technologies with provide connectivity across packaging layers, including chips on boards, boards in backplanes, and shelves within a bay.

articleTitle: MPO-receptacle waveguide device realizing push-on/pull-off fiber attachment to single mode waveguides
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have successfully developed multifibre push on (MPO)-receptacle waveguide device realizing ultimately easy push-on/pull-off fiber attachment to single mode waveguides without index matching. Connection loss is 0.31 dB on the average and direct core-to-core contact has been achieved.

articleTitle: Electrostrictive response in single-mode ring-index profile fibers with large effective mode area
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the theoretical investigation of electrostrictive response of single-mode ring-index profile fibers with a large effective mode area, the results obtained show that the acoustic effect should be taken into account when a large effective mode area fibers are designed for applications in high bit rate systems.

articleTitle: Optical multiplex section level protected network based on point-to-point WDM system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: As an optical layer of large scale IP backbone network, we propose a WDM network with optical multiplex section level protection. A network concept, in which point-to-point systems considered as network elements, is presented.

articleTitle: Mode stabilization technique for the multifrequency laser
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A mode stabilization technique for waveguide grating router lasers which allows suppression of multi-longitudinal mode operation while simultaneously decreasing the laser chip size and increasing the maximum modulation speed is described.

articleTitle: Detailed experimental investigation of an all-active dual-order mode Mach-Zehnder wavelength converter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new all-active DOMO converter has been assessed experimentally at 10 Gbit/s showing almost wavelength-independent performance for signal and CW wavelengths converting the entire EDFA window. Good performance has also been demonstrated at 20 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Polarisation mode dispersion compensation of chirped Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate compensation of polarisation mode dispersion for a chirped Bragg grating. A short length of highly birefringent fiber improves the pulse reshaping action of a chirped Bragg dispersion compensator used in a recirculating loop.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of an evolutionary HFC network architecture for adding narrowcast services
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An evolutionary hybrid-fiber-coal (HFC) network architecture, which does not require DWDM in the beginning stages of adding narrowcast services to broadcast services, is proposed and experimentally verified. It was demonstrated that a directly modulated laser can be used to transport 50 channels of narrowcast signals between 450 and 750 MHz over a transmission distance of 102.5 km to more than 16 optical nodes.

articleTitle: Accelerated aging and reliability studies of multisection tunable GCSR lasers for dense WDM applications
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on the results of an accelerated aging study of tunable grating coupled sampled reflector (GCSR) lasers. Frequency, power and SMSR stability as a function of operation time at elevated temperatures were studied. The effective lifetime of device operation is estimated.

articleTitle: Visualization of fringes in holographic apparatus for fiber Bragg grating fabrication using a phase mask
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A simple apparatus that can be used to monitor the real-time phase, spatial frequency and contrast of the interference pattern in a fiber-grating production environment is described. The apparatus permits rapid production of custom-wavelength fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Low-jitter asynchronous optical packet regenerator using wavelength sampling technique
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Low-jitter, low component complexity, asynchronous optical packet regenerator employing wavelength-domain sampling is proposed. Through simulations we show that this approach features increased jitter tolerance and is ideal for IP-centric applications.

articleTitle: New architectures for CATV networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: New architectures for CATV networks are explored and compared in terms of fiber and amplifiers savings. A computer model was developed to compare the performance and find the optimum placement of amplifiers in the proposed architectures.

articleTitle: Role of fibre in access network for the developing world
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical fiber has already played a major role in reducing the cost of the backbone network making telecom and Internet more affordable in developing countries. This paper examines the role it is now playing in access network resulting into rapid expansion of the network.

articleTitle: Step-wise tunability of a DBR laser with a superimposed fiber grating external cavity
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A DBR laser is step-wise tunable thanks to a superimposed fiber grating external cavity. The stability against tuning current variations in the DBR is excellent. Single-mode operation is achieved with SMSR better than 30 dB.

articleTitle: Influence of polarization dependent loss on birefringent optical fiber networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The addition of polarization dependent losses to birefringent optical networks increases signal distortions. This increase is created by the interaction between polarization mode dispersion and polarization loss. It cannot be explained by either alone.

articleTitle: Impact of cross phase modulation in WDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We discuss the dynamics of cross phase modulation in optical fibers and study the impact of this phenomenon the performance of WDM systems.

articleTitle: Novel ultra-broad-bandwidth electro-optic modulator based on cascaded Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose and evaluate theoretically a novel velocity-matched electro-optic modulator with cascaded Bragg gratings that exhibits V of 1 V and bandwidth in excess of 100 GHz.

articleTitle: COTS fiber optic applications in military and aerospace
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Combining leading-edge fiber optic technology with today's shrinking defense budgets requires innovative solutions incorporating commerical off-the-shelf (COTS) technology. Successful military/aerospace programs include AWACS, in-flight entertainment (IFE), shipboard and fiber optic towed decoys (FOTD). Applications and "lessons learned" will be discussed.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 10 GHz high resolution synchroniser using FBG with wavelength conversion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A synchronisation scheme allowing bit recovery at 10 GHz is presented. Here, a fibre Bragg grating (FBG) in tandem with a wavelength conversion is used to achieve high resolution.

articleTitle: InP-based pin TWA photoreceivers with low group delay scatter over 40 GHz bandwidth
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Advanced 40 Gb/s photoreceiver OEICs, packaged into thermo-stable modules, were developed for 1.55 micron TDM applications. The OEIC comprises a waveguide-integrated photodiode and a traveling wave amplifier with a group delay scatter |/spl plusmn/7 ps| up to 45 GHz.

articleTitle: A novel parallelly-fed traveling wave photodetector with integrated MMI power splitter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a novel velocity matched distributed photodetector (VMDP) with an integrated power splitter to achieve high saturation current. A multimode interference power splitter is used to distribute power equally to the individual detectors of the device, thus increasing the heat induced damage limit. The device is made of MSM type diodes.

articleTitle: Electrically controllable liquid crystal fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel controllable fiber optic filter for broadband rejection is demonstrated by periodically poling liquid crystal core in hollow-core fiber by means of an external long-period-patterned electrode. The theory and experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Highly precise bit-phase synchronization technique for an optically controlled time-division demultiplexer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a new technique for synchronizing, in terms of bit-phase, control pulses to the incoming signal pulses in optically controlled time-division demultiplexers. We demonstrate one hour stable bit-phase synchronization operation with timing error of under 0.7 ps under.

articleTitle: Wavelength label switched IP backbone: architecture and field trial
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The concepts and design of a wavelength label switched (WLS) network is presented. A field trial on an existing four-node fiber network in the Stockholm area is described. The nodes include optical cross-connects used to interconnect high-speed IP routers with reconfigurable wavelength channels.

articleTitle: Optical pulse synthesis using Brillouin selective sideband amplification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a novel concept for Fourier synthesis of optical pulses using Brillouin selective sideband amplification in optical fibers and demonstrate the generation of a 7.8 GHz pulse train using two CW lasers and two phase modulators.

articleTitle: Accurate frequency standard at 1556.2 nm based on a two-photon transition in rubidium for absolute calibration of WDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A high accuracy frequency standard at 1556.2 nm (192.6 THz) is developed for absolute calibration within WDM systems. Measurements of frequency stability of 2.5/spl times/10-13t1/2 and absolute frequency traced down to Cs-primary frequency standard to an accuracy of n/spl tilde/0.5 kHz are presented.

articleTitle: Image transmission through single-mode fibers via shaped coherence functions of low coherent light
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Spatial phase information corresponding a computer generated hologram of a 1D spatial image, which is embedded in the coherence function of low coherence light was transmitted through a single-mode optical fiber and reconstructed with spectral holography.

articleTitle: Novel optical thresholder based on second harmonic generation in long periodically poled lithium niobate for ultrashort pulse optical code division multiple-access
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report a novel yet practical optical thresholding scheme for ultrashort pulse CDMA using second harmonic generation in a long PPLN crystal, with a demonstrated contrast ratio of /spl sim/30 dB and the potential for low power operation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The main design methods, developed so far for the synthesis of fiber Bragg gratings, are reviewed. We particularly focus on a very efficient method based on a differential layer-peeling algorithm and its application to design of high performance gratings.

articleTitle: Increase of photosensitivity in Ge-doped fibers under strain
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
