abstract: The index change produced in Ge-doped fibers by UV light is enhanced by /spl sim/5 when the fiber is strained during UV exposure. This can open a door to faster fabrication of fiber gratings.

articleTitle: A manufacturable WDM tunable source using an integrated laser array
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 12 nm tunable source with 5 mW fiber coupled power is fabricated by integrating four DFB lasers into one output. High-yield and low-cost techniques are used, such as quarter-wave-shifted phase-masks for wavelength definition.

articleTitle: High performance applications for future high performance networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Future networks based on optical technology will enable new, demanding applications that require very high throughput. This talk will describe several such applications and will demonstrate one that involves the testing of an optical MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical systems) device.

articleTitle: Waveguide router subsystems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: WDM creates a market for advanced subsystems such as add-drop multiplexers and crossconnects, tunable and multiwavelength lasers and detectors. Progress in the field of PHASAR-based photonic integrated circuits, the next generation of waveguide router subsystems, is reviewed.

articleTitle: Dispersion mapping in soliton DWDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Dispersion-managed soliton WDM systems exhibit superior transmission quality as soon as Kerr nonlinearity is non negligible. Influence on dispersion mapping is discussed.

articleTitle: New and efficient technique for suppressing the peaks induced, by discrete cladding mode coupling in fiber slanted Bragg grating spectrum
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new design of fiber slanted Bragg grating exhibiting a smooth transmission spectrum without the need of a specific packaging to transform the cladding modes into a continuum of radiation modes is reported.

articleTitle: Cost boundaries for economical OXCs
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Based on the design of ring and mesh network architectures using in-house developed tools, rules are deduced in order to obtain economical solutions for resilient WDM networks based on the use of optical cross-connects (OXCs).

articleTitle: WDM transmission over dispersion shifted fiber in L-band with 25 dB span loss
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Low error rates were obtained from the transmission of twenty 10 Gb/s channels with 100 GHz spacing over four 80 km (25 dB) spans of dispersion shifted fibre (DSF) in the lower wavelength region of the L-band where the effects are largest due to lower dispersion.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of 680 Gbit/s capacity for the medium-haul undersea lightwave cable systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A medium-haul transmission experiment with 680 Gbit/s capacity was demonstrated. Combination of low nonlinear fiber and small dispersion slope fiber is effective to improve the transmission performance, and all channels showed better than 15.5 dB Q-factor.

articleTitle: Measurement of Raman gain coefficient for small wavelength shifts
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Traditionally the calculations of inter-channel power transfer due to stimulated Raman scattering in WDM transmission systems use a wavelength dependence that is a linear approximation of measurements obtained using a 1480 nm pump. We measure the wavelength dependence of the Raman effect for shifts that are typical for the WDM transmission band and use this data to analyze gain tilt in long-haul systems.

articleTitle: Compact optical add-drop multiplexers with low homodyne crosstalk using a single optical circulator and fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate new optical add/drop multiplexer (OADM) architectures with simple and compact configuration and excellent crosstalk performance. The OADM's use a single optical circulator and either one or two narrowband fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Gain flatness of a planar optical waveguide amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report on the broad gain and gain flatness spectra (1530-1565 nm) of a 14 cm long Er/sup 3+/ doped aluminosilicate waveguide amplifier pumped at 1470 nm. We demonstrate its successful use as an in-line amplifier in an 8 channels WDM 155 Mbit/s transmission fiber experiment.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gb/s transmission over 680 km using a fully stabilized 20 channel DBR laser with monolithically integrated semiconductor optical amplifier, photodetector and electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time a fully functional 2.5 Gb/s EA-modulated wavelength-selectable laser module meeting all long-haul transmission requirements for stability, chirp, power and linewidth over 20 channels on a 50 GHz grid. Based on a highly integrated InP chip comprising a DBR laser, semiconductor optical amplifier, power monitor, and EA-modulator, the module also contains optics to ensure simultaneous long-term wavelength and mode stability.

articleTitle: High-speed, low-noise avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A resonant InAlAs-InGaAs avalanche photodiode (APD) that operates at 1 to 1.5 mm has achieved very low noise (k equivalent to 0.18), unity-gain bandwidth of 24 GHz, and a gain-bandwidth-product of 290 GHz.

articleTitle: High-speed TDMA techniques
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: High-speed time division multi-access (TDMA) optical communication systems will be necessary to meet the growing need for bandwidth-on-demand services in local and metropolitan area networks. Recently, many of the technological building blocks necessary to implement such a network have been demonstrated in research laboratories. In this paper, we will review progress towards the realization of TDMA communications systems.

articleTitle: Dual mode operation of semiconductor mode-locked lasers for anti-phase pulse generation
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Anti-phase pulse generation at 40 and 60 GHz have been demonstrated using dual-mode semiconductor mode-locked lasers. Suppression of pulse distortion due to fiber dispersion is confirmed for generated anti-phase pulses.

articleTitle: Capacity-efficient restoration for optical networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Traditional, ring-based restoration reserves half the network capacity for backup. Using generalized loopback, an alternate method for restoration, we show roughly 20% capacity enhancement and investigate tradeoffs between efficient capacity and robustness to double failures.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion tolerance of bandwidth-efficient multilevel modulation schemes
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have identified polarization division multiplex to be advantageous for capacity doubling of fiber spans with a given amplification bandwidth, due to its superior sensitivity, good polarization mode dispersion tolerance and terminal equipment simplicity.

articleTitle: High speed soliton transmission on installed fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We discuss soliton field experiments that have been conducted in Japan, in Europe, and in the US over the past five years. A comparison with soliton laboratory experiments will also be made.

articleTitle: Advantages of nonlinear RZ over NRZ on 10 Gb/s single-span links
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Transmission limits of return-to-zero (RZ) and non-return-to-zero (NRZ) coding are experimentally demonstrated and confirmed by simulation. Power budgets of 60 dB are achieved using either format, however RZ has higher dispersion tolerance. We conclude on a simple explanation of the observed differences.

articleTitle: All-optical subharmonic clock recovery and demultiplexing
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have achieved a phase stabilized an-optical subharmonic clock recovery through a cascading two-stage optical-pulse-injection synchronization of mode-locked diode lasers. Based on this clock recovery scheme, successful 40 to 10 Gbps optical demultiplexing was also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Lensless latching-type fiber switches using silicon micromachined actuators
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Thermally driven latching-type moving-fiber switches without lenses are presented. Silicon micromachined 1/spl times/2, 1/spl times/4 and arrays of 1/spl times/2 switches with high reliability show insertion losses below 1 dB and below /spl sim/60 dB crosstalk.

articleTitle: Micromachined polarization-state controller and its application to polarization-mode dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a lightwave-micromachine-based polarization-controller and experimentally verify its operation. The results suggest that micromachines may be useful in manipulating polarization states in lightwave systems and may thus lead to smaller and cheaper polarization-mode dispersion-compensators.

articleTitle: Eight-channel 40 Gb/s RZ transmission over four 80 km spans (328 km) of NDSF with a net dispersion tolerance in excess of 180 ps/nm
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report experimental results on simultaneous transmission and dispersion compensation of eight wavelengths at 200 GHz channel spacing over 328 km of standard NDSF at 40 Gb/s, using GaAs HBT multiplexer and negative slope dispersion compensators. Individual channel Q values between 7.6 to 8.8 were achieved.

articleTitle: Compact and fully packaged wavelength converter with integrated delay loop for 40 Gbit/s RZ signals
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: First high-speed all-optical wavelength converter, with monolithically integrated delay loop and high extinction-ratio tuning abilities in a simple configuration with only one semiconductor optical amplifier has been realized and successfully tested for 40 Gbit/s RZ format signals.

articleTitle: Recent advances in ultra-wideband Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This talk will review fundamentals of ultra-wideband Raman amplifiers, recent progress of high power pump lasers, and system applications of Raman amplifiers. Pump wavelength determines the gain spectrum of a Raman amplifier. This implies that the gain created by a multi wavelength pumping can have a wideband gain profile, which is approximately described by a linear superposition of each gain by individual pumping, Therefore, in order to realize wideband Raman amplifiers, pump lasers with optimally different wavelengths have to be multiplexed efficiently.

articleTitle: Dependence of coherent crosstalk penalty on the OSNR of the signal
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The in-band crosstalk induced penalty mixed with different signal quality (optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR), extinction ratio) is investigated. Also, tolerant characteristics of the in-band crosstalk induced penalty to the signal quality at optimum decision level is discussed.

articleTitle: Rayleigh noise suppression using a gain flattening filter in a broadband Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel fibre Raman amplifier configuration for reduction of double Rayleigh scattering noise along with gain flattening is proposed It is demonstrated both theoretically and experimentally that an appropriately positioned filter in a single stage amplifier significantly improves Rayleigh noise performance with minimal spontaneous noise penalty.

articleTitle: Variable-bit-rate header recognition for reconfigurable networks using tunable fiber-Bragg-gratings as optical correlators
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate variable-bit-rate recognition of the header information in a data packet. Our technique is reconfigurable for different header sequences and uses optical correlators as look-up tables. We use this optical technique to recognize the header and switch a series of incoming data packets at 155 Mb/s, 622 Mb/s, and 2.5 Gb/s to one of two outputs in a reconfigurable network. Penalty-fee routing with a 1.6 ns guard time is achieved.

articleTitle: The role of DCN in optical WDM networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: With the recent advances in WDM networking technology, and the growing deployment of WDM networking equipment, we are now witnessing the establishment of the next generation networking infrastructure. This paper briefly reviews the role of the data communication network (DCN) in transport networks, and describes MONET's DCN architecture. We then describe a new signalling application of the DCN for WDM-based networks.

articleTitle: New modulation scheme for integrated single side band lightwave source allowing fiber transport up to 256 QAM over 38 GHz carrier
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new modulation scheme for the integrated SSB source is presented allowing now to address 256 QAM modulation format on a 38 GHz millimetric carrier while yielding very low phase noise. Moreover, this scheme presents 10 dB gain for both carrier and signal modulation power.

articleTitle: Convergence of the CRZ and DMS formats in WDM systems using dispersion management
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have carried out simulations to compare the chirped return to zero (CRZ) systems of Bergano et al. (see OFC 1998, paper PD 12) and the dispersion managed soliton (DMS) systems of Favre, et al. (see Electron. Lett., vol. 33, p. 2135, 1997). Our results show remarkable similarities, indicating the convergence of soliton and non-soliton formats in practice.

articleTitle: Recent progress in photonic crystal fibres
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: "holey" photonic crystal fibre (PCF) consists of a thread of glass with microscopic air capillaries running along its length. Its many remarkable properties are overturning the basic precepts of textbook fiber technology.

articleTitle: Performance limits of nonlinear RZ and NRZ coded transmission at 1O and 40 Gb/s on different fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We compare single-channel systems on standard and non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber (NZDSF). Upgrading from NRZ to RZ, the transmission range is increased by 2 to 6 dB. RZ coding balances the benefits of NZDSF over standard fiber at high data rates.

articleTitle: Fully dynamic and reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer on 0.8 nm channel spacing using AOTF and 32-wave tunable LD module
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We developed and confirmed the feasibility of a dynamic optical add drop multiplexer (OADM) system using an acousto optical tunable filter (AOTF) and a wavelength tunable LD module. A 4-concatenation transmission of this system was performed successfully.

articleTitle: High gain and low noise TDFA for 1500 nm band employing novel high concentration doping technique
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a 1500 nm-band thulium-doped fiber amplifier (GS-TDFA) that uses a novel high concentration doping technique, and achieved a gain of beyond 30 dB and a noise figure of around 5 dB in 1480-1510 nm wavelength region. We transmitted eight 10 Gb/s signals ranging from 1483 to 1505 nm, over 120 km long dispersion shifted fibers using proposed GS-TDFA.

articleTitle: Field demonstration of distributed Raman amplification with 3.8 dB Q-improvement for 5/spl times/120 km transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The benefits of distributed Raman amplification are demonstrated in buried cabled field fiber. Performance improvement of 3.8 dB was achieved in a 5/spl times/120 km 10 Gbit/s transmission experiment using 650 mW Raman amplification in each span without apparent damage to the fiber plant.

articleTitle: 53-line multi-wavelength generation of Brillouin/erbium fiber laser with enhanced Stokes feedback coupling
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel laser structure which enables efficient utilization of the laser gain profile and recirculation of Brillouin shifted signals inside the cavity. Multi-wavelength operation of more than 53 Stokes lines has been obtained with excellent flatness and stability. Procedures for optimum operation conditions will be described.

articleTitle: OMS protection scheme implementation in the PEGASO OTN testbed
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper presents the OMS protection in the PEGASO testbed in line with the optical transport network (OTN) defined in ITU-T Rec. G.872. Optical signal protection time, OAM signaling and DCN restoration are described.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration in IP over WDM access networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper examines a high-speed IP over WDM access network. The performance benefits of dynamically allocating wavelengths to access routers are examined and compared with static wavelength allocation. It is shown that dynamic reconfiguration can significantly improve network performance.

articleTitle: Improving performance using waveguide filter and optimal probe and signal powers for all-optical wavelength conversion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Reports the improved extinction ratio of the output signal for 80 km G.652 or 240 km G.655 SMF transmission experiments in terms of an all-optical wavelength converter based on XGM in a SOA at 10 Gb/s by using a waveguide filter, optimal probe and signal powers and a DCF compensator.

articleTitle: Low-loss polarisation-independent dynamic gain-equalisation filter
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel dynamic gain equalisation filter is described. Extinction tuning is by variable Faraday rotator. Wavelength tuning is by temperature control of a waveplate. It is suitable for active gain control of optically amplified systems.

articleTitle: Automatic wavelength channel-by-channel equalizer
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a wavelength equalizer that can automatically control individual channel powers in a 40 channel system, yet gives no distortion to channels that already have the same power as their neighbors. It has <6.8 dB insertion loss over 32 nm, 9-13 dB attenuation range, and <0.18 dB polarization/time-dependent loss.

articleTitle: High-speed InGaAsP electroabsorption modulators: dependence of the device characteristics on the mesa design
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present characteristics of InGaAsP electroabsorption modulators with variable length and mesa width. We demonstrate devices with return loss below -10 dB, bandwidth above 40 GHz and extinction ratio of 10 dB/2 V. We show that low capacitance is advantageous for high-speed operation even when achieved at the expense of increased series resistance.

articleTitle: New dispersion compensating fibres for simultaneous compensation of dispersion and dispersion slope of non-zero dispersion shifted fibres in the C or L band
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new dispersion compensating fiber with extremely high negative dispersion slope is reported. Low insertion loss between 1530 and 1610 nm is demonstrated using a new splice technique.

articleTitle: Simple technique to determine cross-phase modulation induced penalties in WDM transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A simple technique using measured or calculated cross-phase modulation distortion of a CW channel to predict transmission penalties is presented. The accuracy of this method is demonstrated with direct BER measurements of 10 Gbit/s WDM channels for a range of distances using a recirculating loop.

articleTitle: 128/spl times/10.66 Gbit/s transmission over 840 km standard SMF with 140 km optical repeater spacing (30.4 dB loss) employing dual-band distributed Raman amplification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the first demonstration of a high-capacity (1.28 Tbit/s), long-haul (6/spl times/140 km) WDM transmission employing dual-band (C/L-band) distributed Raman amplification (DRA). The DRA improved OSNR and enabled an extra-long repeater spacing of 140 km.

articleTitle: Enhanced wavelength resolution chromatic dispersion measurements using fixed sideband technique
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We describe a new chromatic dispersion measurement technique that enables sub-picosecond timing and sub-picometer wavelength accuracy simultaneously. Experimental results comparing the new measurement technique with the standard modulation phase shift are shown.

articleTitle: Demonstration of distributed mesh restoration and auto-provisioning in a WDM network using a large optical cross-connect
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report the first demonstration of distributed restoration and auto-provisioning for the WDM mesh network, using four nodes, five links, and twelve 2.5 Gb/s unidirectional demands. The measured restoration time is <50 ms.

articleTitle: Net gain of 15.5 dB from a 5.1 cm long Er/sup 3+/-doped phosphate glass fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: New erbium-doped phosphate glasses and fibers were fabricated. A net gain of 15.5 dB at 1535 was achieved from 5.1 cm long fiber, which represents the highest gain per unit length for fiber amplifiers to the best of our knowledge.

articleTitle: Demonstration of virtually-imaged phased-array device for tunable dispersion compensation in 16/spl times/10 Gb/s WDM transmission over 480 km standard fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A tunable dispersion compensation device based on a virtually-imaged phased-array technology with greater than 50 nm optical bandwidth is demonstrated and compared to DCF in a WDM experiment transmitting 16/spl times/10 Gb/s NRZ signals over 6/spl times/80 km of conventional fiber.

articleTitle: Low-noise 1-watt Er/Yb fiber amplifier for CATV distribution in HFC and FTTH/C systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A low-noise l-W cladding-pumped Er/Yb fiber amplifier amplifies analog video signals from a 50 km super trunk and delivers them to 256 fiber nodes in a standard HFC architecture or 512 fiber nodes in a FTTH/C system.

articleTitle: Highly efficient 1 Tb/s (50 ch/spl times/20 Gb/s)-2000 km RZ transmission experiment by suppressing XPM with optimized pulsewidth
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: High spectral efficiency was realized in 20 Gbit/s-based DWDM experiment by manipulating the pulsewidth to suppress XPM. In the optimum pulsewidth 25 ps case, 50 ch/spl times/2O Gbit/s signals were transmitted 2000 km in a high local dispersion-managed line with high spectral efficiency of 0.4 bit/s/Hz.

articleTitle: PMD characterization techniques
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Random birefringence causing transmission impairments in optical fibers is characterized by first- and second-order polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) vectors. These are measured by time domain or frequency domain techniques. Results showing low-noise high-resolution PMD data are described.

articleTitle: Polarization-insensitive parametric wavelength converter based on cascaded nonlinearities in LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguides
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We developed a polarization-independent wavelength converter using periodically poled LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguides. The device uses a pump in the 1.5 mm band, has negligible polarization sensitivity and a penalty of less than 0.5 dB at 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Characteristics of sampled grating DBR lasers with integrated semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A state-of-the-art demonstration of photonic integration with results illustrating integrated widely-tunable lasers capable of high output power (>8 dBm), wide tuning ranges (50-70 nm), and modulation (2.488 Gb/s) is presented.

articleTitle: Adaptive chromatic dispersion controller based on an electro-optically chirped arrayed-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose an electro-optically chirped arrayed-waveguide grating for adaptive chromatic dispersion control. Simulations show /spl plusmn/4460 ps/nm compensation for a 8.8 mm active-section length LiNbO/sub 3/ device. Typical operating voltage is <10 V with 10 /spl mu/m electrode spacing.

articleTitle: Broadband gain flattened Raman amplifier to extend operation in the third telecommunication window
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report the gain flattening of dual stage dual wavelength pumped fibre Raman amplifiers flattening the gain using long period fibre grating and a first order interferometric filter. A flattened gain of 60 nm and an average gain of 15.9 dB were achieved.

articleTitle: A simple and robust high-speed wavelength converter using fiber cross-phase modulation and filtering
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: 40 Gbit/s RZ data wavelength conversion is demonstrated using cross-phase modulation in an optical fiber with subsequent conversion of phase modulation to amplitude modulation using an optical filter. The scheme is potentially ultra high speed and can be made polarization independent.

articleTitle: KEOPS optical packet switch demonstrator: architecture and testbed performance
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: This paper reviews the overall performance of a fully equipped 4/spl times/4 optical packet switch implemented as the European ACTS KEOPS project demonstrator. Schemes for contention resolution and a service differentiation consistent with the demonstrator architecture are discussed.

articleTitle: 4O-Gbit/s transport system: its WDM upgrade
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The state of the art of transmission technologies for 40 Gbit/s/channel transport system is described. 40 Gbit/s system prototype and N/spl times/40 Gbit/s WDM transmission performance of a new modulation format are presented.

articleTitle: High power diode pumped single-transverse-mode Yb fiber laser operating at 978 nm
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A single-mode Yb fiber laser delivering 450 mW at 978 nm is reported. The device consists of a tapered multimode Yb fiber pumped with a 2 W 920 nm broadstripe. The pumping scheme has advantages over double-clad fiber lasers when applied to 3-level laser systems.

articleTitle: 150/sup +/ channel ultra-DWDM source with N/spl times/10 GHz spacing utilizing longitudinal mode slicing of supercontinuum
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report a 150+ channel ultra-DWDM source utilizing longitudinal mode slicing of a 140 nm supercontinuum. The modes of source laser are replicated in 48 nm region with /spl plusmn/0.5 dB uniformity, precise N/spl times/10 GHz spacing and <7 dB/Hz RIN degradation.

articleTitle: Backbone network architectures for IP optical networking
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Novel service layer (IP/MPLS) and transport layer (SONET/SDH, WDM) network architectures are analyzed and compared for IP backbones, considering multiple parameters: network capacity, cost, restoration strategy, reconfigurability and accommodation of preemptable traffic. The results show the value of networking in multi-terabit IP backbones.

articleTitle: Control of waveguide properties in hybrid polymer-silica microstructured optical fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We investigate the properties of Bragg gratings in hybrid polymer-silica microstructured fibers and show the ability to design waveguide and polymer properties to control fiber grating spectral characteristics, including suppression and temperature tuning of core-cladding mode coupling.

articleTitle: All-optical time-slot-interchange and wavelength conversion using difference-frequency-generation and FBGs
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous all optical time-slot-interchange and wavelength conversion of a 2.5 Gb/s bit stream. We used different frequency generation (DFG) as a wavelength converter and fibre Bragg gratings (FBG)s as optical buffers. This technique is reconfigurable, scalable and employs high-extinction-ratio DFG-based time-slot-switching.

articleTitle: A new scheme for all-optical signal reshaping based on wavelength conversion in optical fibers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We theoretically demonstrate for the first time that, if four wave mixing in fibers is properly optimized, wavelength-converted signals can exhibit excellent intensity-noise cancellation. Numerical simulations confirm almost complete suppression of intensity fluctuations.

articleTitle: Dependence of L-band amplifier efficiency on pump wavelength and amplifier design
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An improvement in amplifier efficiency resulting from pump wavelength tuning is shown to occur in extended band (L-band) EDFAs. We investigate the effects for different EDFA configurations and for 980 nm and 1480 nm pumping.

articleTitle: The merit of shared and dedicated protection WDM rings in a hybrid network design
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We compare network designs based on stacked dedicated and shared protection WDM rings, considering different cost scenarios and traffic patterns. The results reveal the merit of combining both ring types in a hybrid network design.

articleTitle: Compact, in-line, all-fiber polarimeter using fiber gratings
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a compact, low loss, low cost in-fiber polarimeter using a UV induced waveplate and fiber gratings. The polarimeter has accuracy comparable to commercial devices, is wavelength insensitive over 70 nm, and is tested in control loop that actively stabilizes a random input polarization.

articleTitle: Effect of modulational instability on broadband wavelength conversion using four-wave mixing in optical fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show that, in fiber-optic four-wave mixing based wavelength conversion, modulational instability compensates for the flatness degradation of the conversion efficiency due to birefringence. A 76 nm ultra-broadband 1 dB highly-flattened wavelength conversion with conversion efficiency up to /spl sim/4 dB is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A system for native Ethernet optical transport at 10 Gb/s
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The first system to transport native Ethernet data at a serial rate of 1O Gb/s is reported. Up to 8 asynchronous gigabit Ethernet signals are multiplexed to 10 Gb/s and directly modulate a Fabry-Perot laser at 1310 nm for 2-8 km transport over standard single-mode fiber.

articleTitle: Wavelength monitoring in DWDM networks using low cost semiconductor laser diode/amplifiers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple wavelength monitoring technique using the transparency detection of low-cost semiconductor laser diode/amplifiers to have sub-angstrom resolution and good stability that can meet the requirements of dense wavelength-division-multiplexing systems.

articleTitle: Strictly non-blocking N/spl times/N thermo-capillarity optical matrix switch using silica-based waveguide
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose a silica-based strictly non-blocking N/spl times/N thermo-capiliarity optical matrix switch. The feasibility of 2-dimensional batch oil injection and multilayered wiring were confirmed by type 16/spl times/16 optical matrix switch.

articleTitle: 32/spl times/20 Gb/s transmission over trans-Atlantic distance (6200 km) with 31% spectral efficiency
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present the first experimental demonstration of trans-Atlantic transmission using DWDM 20 Gb/s channels. A total capacity of 640 Gb/s (32/spl times/20 Gb/s) was transmitted 6200 km with a spectral efficiency of 31 %.

articleTitle: Optical path and crosstalk monitoring for optical cross-connect switches using arrayed waveguide grating
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an optical path monitoring scheme for optical cross connects using arrayed waveguide grating as multiplexer/demultiplexer based on their periodicity and routing properties. Partial failure induced crosstalk in switches can also be monitored.

articleTitle: A simple compensator for high order polarization mode dispersion effects
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present a PMD compensator for the rotation of the principal states with frequency. It requires only two control parameters more than existing first order compensators. The compensation for first order is decoupled from the compensation for high orders and is controlled independently.

articleTitle: Digital optical processing
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Optical digital processing is a key technology that will allow advanced functionality to be obtainable directly at the optical layer in future photonic networks. Recent progress in all-optical functional circuits will be discussed.

articleTitle: Temperature stabilized tunable fiber grating devices with integrated on-fiber thin film heaters
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple approach to stabilized control of thermally tuned fiber grating devices that use integrated thin film resistive heaters. This technique exploits the temperature dependence of the resistance of the integrated heater as a sensors to accurately and continuously measure the fiber temperature.

articleTitle: Network demonstration of 32/spl lambda//spl times/10 Gb/s across 6 nodes of 640/spl times/640 WSXCs with 750 km Raman-amplified fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Long-haul transmission across six 640/spl times/640 (320 working+320 protection) wavelength-selective cross-connects, interconnected by six 125 km spans of Raman-amplified NZ-DSF fiber using 32 wavelengths at 10 Gb/s, is reported. System configuration, and optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR) and Q performances are presented.

articleTitle: 168 Gbps error-free demultiplexing with hybrid-integrated symmetric Mach-Zehnder all-optical switch
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The symmetric Mach-Zehnder (SMZ) all-optical switch is quite promising for various types of future high-speed all-optical processing. We have developed a hybrid-integrated SMZ all-optical switch and achieved the error-free demultiplexing of 168 Gbps data pulses.

articleTitle: Advanced fibre Bragg gratings for high performance dispersion compensation in DWDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We present experimental results of fiber Bragg gratings designed by inverse-scattering for dispersion compensating 80 km of standard fiber on a 50 GHz grid the device offers significantly improved bandwidth utilisation and dispersion linearity over conventional designs.

articleTitle: Protection cycle covers in optical networks with arbitrary mesh topologies
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A new methodology of finding cycle covers in networks with arbitrary mesh topologies is presented. The cycles that comprise the cycle cover are then used to protect the network against link and node failures.

articleTitle: Cascaded semiconductor optical amplifiers for transmission of 32 DWDM channels over 315 km
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Cascaded semiconductor optical amplifiers are used as in-line amplifiers for error free transmission of 32 signal channels at 2.3 Gbit/s over 315 km of AllWave/sup TM/.

articleTitle: Stimulated Raman scattering cancellation in wavelength-division-multiplexed systems via spectral inversion
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We theoretically demonstrate that stimulated Raman scattering crosstalk in wavelength-division-multiplexed systems can be totally eliminated using spectral inversion techniques. This result is always true irrespective of the specific Raman loss/gain profile of the fiber system.

articleTitle: Dynamic behavior in L-band EDFA
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have measured the dynamic behavior of a two-stage L-Band EDFA. The response time constants are about 105 /spl mu/s and 260 /spl mu/s when one and seven out of eight channels were dropped accordingly and the amplifier was well saturated. These values were about four and five times larger than what were observed in a C-Band EDFA. The difference can be explained by the different intrinsic saturation power in these two bands.

articleTitle: 400 Gb/s transmission (40 Ch./spl times/10 Gb/s) over 544 km from a spectrum-sliced supercontinuum source
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We report the error-free transmission over 544 km of standard fiber of 40 channels at 9.953 Gb/s from a spectrum-sliced supercontinuum source. All but three of the transmitted channels have error floors better than log(BER)=/spl sim/16.

articleTitle: Fused taper fibre microcoupler
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Single-mode fibre couplers considerably less than 1 mm long are formed by fusing together two tapered fibres using a carbon dioxide laser. This will allow a miniature version of many all-fibre devices to be made.

articleTitle: Unification and extension of the traffic-grooming problem in WDM ring networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The traffic-grooming problem multiplexes smaller-rate traffic streams into higher-rate streams using the smallest number of SONET add-drop multiplexers (S-ADMs). By unifying and extending previous work, two new approaches-single-hop and multi-hop-are introduced and evaluated.

articleTitle: Record 1 watt fiber-coupled-power 1480 nm diode laser pump for Raman and erbium doped fiber amplification
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We reported the first 1 watt fiber-coupled flared diode laser and a record 475 mW fiber-coupled narrow-stripe diode laser at 1480 nm and demonstrate distributed Raman gain up to 22 dB and 14 dB margin improvement.

articleTitle: Dynamic routing, rearrangement, and defragmentation in WDM ring networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Simulation studies of dynamic routing with rearrangement in WDM ring networks indicate that up to five addition paths maybe accommodated with 16 wavelengths. Dynamic alteration of a wavelength is necessary to achieve this.

articleTitle: Impact of PMD on FWM crosstalk in WDM systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: The impact of polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) on four-wave mixing crosstalk in wavelength division multiplexed fiber systems is quantified experimentally. The benefit of using polarization-multiplexed channels for suppression of crosstalk is reduced for links with even modest PMD.

articleTitle: Impact of source spontaneous emission (SSE) on the measurement of DWDM components
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a tunable laser source with strongly reduced source spontaneous emission (SSE) when applied to critical DWDM-components.

articleTitle: Variable attenuation slope compensator (VASC) using silica-based planar lightwave circuit technology for active gain slope control in EDFAs
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A novel planar lightwave circuit device called variable attenuation slope compensator (VASC) is proposed for active gain slope control in EDFAs. Its attenuation slope is electrically controllable with the average attenuation unchanged.

articleTitle: Complexity and performance comparisons between optical OOK-CDMA chip-level receivers and double-optical-hardlimiters correlation receivers
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show that chip-level receivers (recently proposed) are much simpler and more practical than traditional double-optical-hardlimiters correlation receivers in demultiplexing optical CDMA signals. Further, we show that the bit error rates of both receivers are competitive to each other.

articleTitle: Histogram method for identification and evaluation of crosstalk
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Signal performance monitoring by a novel histogram method is proposed for identification crosstalk, it is based on a deconvolution method. Measured histograms for signals with inband crosstalk are investigated and the BER is successfully estimated.

articleTitle: Optical networking with reconfigurable access nodes in the NGI ONRAMP test bed
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have built reconfigurable access nodes for the next generation Internet (NGI) ONRAMP test bed and used them to demonstrate basic optical networking functionality, including over a 100 km installed fiber link.

articleTitle: Cross phase modulation in discrete Raman amplifiers and its reduction
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We fabricated an optimized discrete Raman amplifier with dispersion compensating fibre (DCF) and evaluated its nonlinearities. XPM is larger than in a comparable EDFA. By simulations, we revealed methods to reduce XPM substantially, which is beneficial for wideband WDM systems.

articleTitle: Narrow-band acousto-optic tunable filter fabricated from highly uniform tapered optical fiber
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: A 2.9 nm bandwidth AOTF was fabricated from highly uniform, tapered optical fiber. The filter had an excess loss of 0.02 dB, >20 dB extinction, was polarization insensitive, and had the smallest bandwidth-length product reported to date.

articleTitle: PMD-induced reduction of nonlinear penalties in terrestrial optical fiber transmission
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We simulated optical fiber transmission with large PMD using realistic parameters. We found that nonlinearly-induced chirp coupled to second-order PMD tan lead to a penalty reduction.

articleTitle: Simple IP restoration for IP/GbE/10 GbE optical networks
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: IP and Ethernet are the dominant transport and link-layer protocols in data networks. In this paper we demonstrate how IP can be used to provide reliable Ethernet transport with fast restoration performance comparable with that achieved in SONET networks.

articleTitle: 210 Gbit/s (10.7 Gbit/s/spl times/21 WDM) transmission over 1200 km with 200 km repeater spacing for the festoon undersea cable system
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have demonstrated 210 bit/s (10.7 Gbit/s/spl times/21 WDM) transmission over 1200 km with ultra long repeater spacing of 200 km with proper dispersion management together with Raman amplifier and EDFA for the festoon type undersea cable network. We obtained a Q-factor for all channels greater than 15.6 dB.

articleTitle: Accurate measurements of erbium-doped fiber amplifier gain spectra
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We show that a wide-band noise source can be used to accurately measure the large-signal gain spectrum of an EDFA. Even in a range where spectral hole burning has a significant impact. Data is presented for a comparison of our technique, with the more conventional method.

articleTitle: 1580 nm band erbium-doped fiber amplifier employing novel temperature compensation technique
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have developed a novel two-stage configuration of a 1580 nm band erbium-doped fiber amplifier employing temperature compensation technique. Gain flatness less than 1.0 dB over 30 nm is successfully achieved from 0/spl deg/C and 70/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Optical SCM data extraction using a fiber loop mirror for WDM network systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a polarization independent dual-port filter to extract SCM data from a WDM baseband SCM channel using a fiber loop-mirror filter. Suppressed carrier detection eliminates dispersion induced fading in the SCM channel and enables data recovery using simple photodetection for multiple WDM channels.

articleTitle: Superimposed in-fiber grating structures for optical signal processing in wavelength-division-multiplexing systems
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We design superimposed in-fiber grating structures to work as multi-channel real-time optical spectrum analyzers for wavelength-division-multiplexing applications. The potential applications of the technique proposed here, as well as extensions to other signal treatments, are also analyzed.

articleTitle: 4/spl times/10 Gb/s terrestrial optical free space transmission over 1.2 km using an EDFA preamplifier with 100 GHz channel spacing
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: We have transmitted 4/spl times/10 Gb/s channels over 1.2 km free space with the 1OO GHz channel spacing. Focusing the transmitted beam into the single-mode fiber, we could use conventional devices including an EDFA at the receiver.

articleTitle: LiNbO/sub 3/ optical single-sideband modulator
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: An LiNbO/sub 3/ SSB modulator was fabricated by integrating four phase-modulator waveguides, an asymmetric cross junction, and a sideband-suppression gate. The demonstration of the SSB modulation and the expectation of future applications are described.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of Bragg grating based DFB fiber lasers operating above 1610 nm
publicationTitle: Optical Fiber Communication Conference. Technical Digest Postconference Edition. Trends in Optics and Photonics Vol.37 (IEEE Cat. No. 00CH37079)
abstract: Distributed feedback fiber lasers operating at wavelengths above the L-band an presented for the first time. Furthermore, a numerical analysis that predicts the optimum design of these lasers has been developed.
